definition_zh: 煮沸；沸腾；煮（食物）；（口语）发怒
definition_en: to heat a liquid until it bubbles, to cook food in boiling water, or to be very angry
core_image: 锅里翻腾的水和上升的白汽
scene: 厨房里，锅中的水开始翻滚，白色蒸汽升到窗上。 The water in the pot began to boil.
sceneCN: 这里 boil 是「沸腾」（第 2 个义项：液体受热翻滚）；句意为锅里的水开始沸腾。

pos.zh: 动词：煮沸；沸腾；煮；（口语）发怒

derivatives.zh: 由 boil 加 -er 构成，义为「锅炉；热水器」
由 boil 加 -ing 构成，义为「沸腾的；极热的」
由 hard 与 boiled 组合而成，义为「煮得全熟的；硬心肠的」

senses.title: To heat a liquid
senses.definition: to heat a liquid until it reaches the temperature where it bubbles strongly
senses.definitionCN: 把液体加热到强烈冒泡的温度
senses.example: She boiled the water for tea.
senses.exampleCN: 她烧开水泡茶。
senses.why: Latin bulla meant a bubble, and boiling is exactly the moment when bubbles rise through a liquid.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 bulla 意为「气泡」，而沸腾正是气泡从液体里升起的时刻。

senses.title: To bubble with heat
senses.definition: used of a liquid: to bubble and turn to steam when heated
senses.definitionCN: 用于液体：受热时冒泡并变成蒸汽
senses.example: The soup is boiling on the stove.
senses.exampleCN: 汤在炉子上沸腾。
senses.why: The same event is seen from the liquid's side, so the verb also works without an object.
senses.whyCN: 同一件事也可以从液体这一边看，所以这个动词也能不带宾语。

senses.title: To cook in water
senses.definition: to cook food by keeping it in water that is boiling
senses.definitionCN: 把食物放在沸腾的水中煮熟
senses.example: He boiled two eggs for breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 他煮了两个鸡蛋当早餐。
senses.why: Boiling water is the oldest cooking tool, so the verb moved from the water to the food in it.
senses.whyCN: 沸水是最古老的烹饪工具，于是这个动词从水移到水里的食物。

senses.title: To be furious
senses.definition: to be extremely angry, used in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 极度愤怒，多用于口语
senses.example: He was boiling when he heard the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到这个消息时他怒不可遏。
senses.why: Anger is felt as heat rising inside, so boiling became a picture of furious emotion.
senses.whyCN: 愤怒被感受为体内升起的热，于是「沸腾」成了暴怒的画面。

intro.en: Boil goes back through French to Latin words for a bubble, and the bubble is still visible in its meaning.
intro.cn: boil 经法语可追溯到拉丁语中表示「气泡」的词，气泡至今仍留在它的词义里。

items.en: Latin bulla meant a bubble or a round object, the picture behind the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bulla 意为气泡或圆形物，这是整个词族的画面来源。

items.en: The verb bullire meant to bubble, and it described liquid rising in round bursts.
items.cn: 动词 bullire 意为冒泡，描述液体成团上涌的样子。

items.en: Old French turned the Latin verb into boillir, still meaning to boil or bubble.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁动词变成 boillir，仍表示煮沸或冒泡。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the verb as boilen, first for liquid and then for cooking.
items.cn: 中古英语借入动词 boilen，先用于液体，后用于烹饪。

items.en: Today boil covers heating liquid, bubbling, cooking and, informally, furious anger.
items.cn: 今天 boil 覆盖加热液体、冒泡、烹饪以及口语中的暴怒。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in shape; the near-meaning group collects other cooking and heat words.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写接近的词；近义组收其他烹饪与加热的词。

entries.definition: A device that heats water for a building or a machine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「锅炉；热水器」，由 boil 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: A thick liquid used for cooking or machines.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「油」，读音与 boil 接近。

entries.definition: A length of wire wound into rings.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「线圈」，读音与 boil 接近。

entries.definition: To cook slowly just below the boiling point.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「小火慢煮」，温度略低于沸点。

entries.definition: To cook food with the hot vapour of boiling water.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「蒸」，用沸水产生的热蒸汽烹饪。

entries.definition: A ball of air or gas in a liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「气泡」，正是 boil 词源里的那个画面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded history, the real family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Latin bulla meant a bubble, and boiling is the moment bubbles rise through liquid.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 bulla 意为气泡，而沸腾正是气泡从液体中升起的时刻。

normal.en: Old French boillir and Middle English boilen carry the same meaning forward.
normal.cn: 古法语 boillir 与中古英语 boilen 一路把这个意思传下来。

normal.en: Boiling water is the oldest cooking tool, so the verb moved from water to food.
normal.cn: 沸水是最古老的烹饪工具，所以动词从水移到食物。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with water, egg, point and over.
normal.cn: 它常与 water、egg、point、over 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-o-i-l; the oi gives the sound of coin.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-o-i-l，中间的 oi 读得像 coin 里的音。

abstract.en: See bubbles climb through a pot and white steam reach the window: that is boil.
abstract.cn: 想象气泡从锅里升起，白色蒸汽爬到窗上：那就是 boil。

abstract.en: Let the same heat rise inside a person and the word becomes anger.
abstract.cn: 让同样的热在一个人体内升起，这个词就变成了愤怒。

abstract.en: Say the word and let the rising bubbles bring the sense back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那些上升的气泡把意思带回来。

examples.cn: 她烧开水泡茶。

examples.en: The soup is boiling on the stove.
examples.cn: 汤在炉子上沸腾。

examples.en: He boiled two eggs for breakfast.
examples.cn: 他煮了两个鸡蛋当早餐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「波伊尔」——锅里冒起一串气泡：煮沸

root: boil 经古法语 boillir 追溯到拉丁语 bullire（冒泡），而 bullire 又来自 bulla（气泡）。中古英语借入作 boilen，先用于液体受热翻滚，再用于把食物放在沸水里煮。现代英语里，这个动词还用来表示体内热感升腾的暴怒。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of boil rest on one picture: heat making bubbles rise, whether in a pot, in food, or inside an angry person.
sensesIntro.cn: boil 的四个义项都立在同一个画面上：热让气泡升起，无论在锅里、在食物里，还是在愤怒的人体内。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bubbles climbing through a pot while steam rises
core.cn: 核心意象：气泡从锅里升起，蒸汽同时上腾

branches.en: THE HEAT: heating a liquid until it bubbles is the plainest sense.
branches.cn: 加热线：把液体加热到冒泡是最朴素的义项。

branches.en: THE BUBBLES: the liquid's own bubbling is the same event seen from inside.
branches.cn: 气泡线：液体自身的翻滚是同一事件从内部看到的样子。

branches.en: THE POT: boiling water became the oldest way to cook food.
branches.cn: 锅线：沸水成了最古老的烹饪方式。

branches.en: THE TEMPER: rising heat inside a person pictures furious anger.
branches.cn: 脾气线：体内升起的热，比喻暴怒。

branches.en: THE STATE: heating and bubbling are two views of one moment.
branches.cn: 状态线：加热与冒泡是同一时刻的两种视角。

intro.en: Boil is a base verb with a small noun use, so the items below are its endings and the words it joins.
intro.cn: boil 是基础动词，另有少量名词用法，下面列出的是它的词尾以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin bulla and bullire are the recorded source words of this family, and they are given here as the Latin layer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 bulla 与 bullire 是这个词族有记录的来源词，此处作为拉丁语层列出。

items.example: Boilen is the recorded Middle English form.
items.exampleCN: boilen 是有记录的中古英语形式。

items.meaning: an oval food from a hen

definition_zh: 中心；中央；中心点；（活动、兴趣的）核心
definition_en: the middle point or part of something; the place where activity is strongest
core_image: 圆心：圆上每一点到它的距离都相等
scene: 小镇广场四周是老房子，中间立着一座钟楼。 The clock tower stands right at the centre of our town square.
sceneCN: 这里 centre 是「中心」（第 1 个义项：正中间的点）；句意是钟楼立在广场正中心。

derivatives.zh: 由 centre 加 -al 构成，义为「中心的；主要的」
由 central 加 -ly 构成，义为「在中心地」
由 con- 加 centr 构成，义为「集中；专心」

senses.title: The middle point
senses.definition: the point that is the same distance from every edge
senses.definitionCN: 与各边缘距离相等的那个点
senses.example: Draw a red dot at the centre of the circle.
senses.exampleCN: 在圆心画一个红点。
senses.why: The word names the balancing point of a shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指一个形状的平衡点。

senses.title: A place where activity happens
senses.definition: a place or building where people gather for an activity
senses.definitionCN: 人们为某活动聚集的地方或建筑
senses.example: The new sports centre opens on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 新体育中心周一开放。
senses.why: Where people gather, a building soon gets the name centre.
senses.whyCN: 人们聚集之处，建筑便被称为中心。

senses.title: The main focus of interest
senses.definition: the person or thing that gets the most attention
senses.definitionCN: 最受关注的人或事物
senses.example: She was the centre of attention at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 她是聚会上众人关注的焦点。
senses.why: Attention, like circles, gathers around one middle point.
senses.whyCN: 注意力像圆一样，聚拢在一个中心点。

intro.en: Centre traces back to the needle of a drawing compass.
intro.cn: centre 的源头是画圆用圆规的针尖。

items.en: Greek kentron means a sharp point, the needle that holds a compass still.
items.cn: 希腊语 kentron 意为「尖点」，即固定圆规的针尖。

items.en: Latin wrote it centrum and used it for the middle point of a circle.
items.cn: 拉丁语写作 centrum，指圆的中心点。

items.en: Old French carried it as centre into the languages of Europe.
items.cn: 古法语以 centre 的形式把它传入欧洲各语言。

items.en: English adopted centre in the fourteenth century for geometry and the middle of things.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 centre，用于几何和事物的中部。

items.en: American spelling later preferred center; both mean the same.
items.cn: 美式拼写后来用 center；两者含义相同。

note.en: Centre has many neighbours in shape and in meaning.
note.cn: centre 在形状和意义上都有许多邻居。

entries.definitionCN: 中心的（centre 的形容词）

entries.definition: to bring to one centre
entries.definitionCN: 集中

entries.definition: one hundred years; shares the cent- shape
entries.definitionCN: 世纪（拼写相近同根）

entries.definition: a smell; sounds the same but starts with s
entries.definitionCN: 气味（发音相同，拼写仅多 s，词源不同）

entries.definition: the middle part of something
entries.definitionCN: 中间

entries.definition: the most important central part
entries.definitionCN: 核心；心脏部位

entries.definition: a central place where activity gathers
entries.definitionCN: 枢纽；活动中心

entries.definition: the point where attention gathers
entries.definitionCN: 焦点

normalIntro.en: centr- is the stem; the endings change the job.
normalIntro.cn: centr- 是词干；后缀改变词的职能。

normal.en: centre = centre point of a circle.
normal.cn: centre 是圆的中心点。

normal.en: central = centr + -al, like the centre.
normal.cn: central 由 centr 加 -al 构成，中心的。

normal.en: concentrate = con- + centr, pull to one centre.
normal.cn: concentrate 由 con- 加 centr 构成，聚到同一中心。

normal.en: city centre is the busiest middle part of a city.
normal.cn: city centre 是城市最繁忙的中心地带。

normal.en: centre sounds like sent with an r.
normal.cn: centre 读起来像 sent 加了 r。

abstract.en: Picture the clock tower standing exactly in the middle of the square.
abstract.cn: 想象钟楼正立于广场中央。

abstract.en: Picture a busy mall called a shopping centre.
abstract.cn: 想象一座被称为购物中心的繁忙商场。

abstract.en: Picture every eye in the room turned to one person.
abstract.cn: 想象满屋子目光都投向同一个人。

examples.en: Please stand at the centre of the circle and hold the rope.
examples.cn: 请站在圆心拉着绳子。

examples.en: The shopping centre is closed on Mondays.
examples.cn: 购物中心周一闭馆。

examples.en: Our city has built a big sports centre near the river.
examples.cn: 我们城市在河边建了一座大型体育中心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「森特」——森林中央有一座特别的塔， everybody 都往那儿走，它是中心，所以叫「森特」。

sensesIntro.en: From a point on paper to a place and a focus.
sensesIntro.cn: 从纸上的一个点到一处场所、一个焦点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the middle point of everything
core.cn: 核心意象：一切的中点

branches.en: Geometry and location
branches.cn: 几何与位置

branches.en: Buildings and gathering
branches.cn: 建筑与聚集

branches.cn: 关注与焦点

branches.en: The middle of things and minds
branches.cn: 事物与思维的中点

branches.en: Places people care about
branches.cn: 人们关心的场所

intro.cn: 学会 centr-，一个词族随之打开。

latinIntro.en: Latin centrum anchors this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 centrum 支撑着这一词族。

items.example: Centre in Britain, center in America.
items.exampleCN: 英国拼 centre，美国拼 center。

items.example: The office is in a central street.

items.meaning: to draw together at one point

items.example: Concentric circles share the same centre.
The wheel looks a little eccentric.
items.exampleCN: 这个轮子看起来有点偏心。

items.example: A spin dryer uses centrifugal force.
The rope pulls the ball in a centripetal way.
items.exampleCN: 绳子以向心方式拉着球。

definition_zh: 穿、戴；磨损、穿旧；耐穿；名词：磨损；衣着
definition_en: to have clothes on the body, to damage something by long use, or the damage caused by use
core_image: 一件外套的袖口被日日挽起，布料薄了、起了毛
scene: 冬天的早晨，她在门口匆匆披上大衣，围巾绕了两圈。 He wore the same grey coat all winter and never complained.
sceneCN: 这里 wear 是「穿、戴」（第 1 个义项：把衣物穿在身上）；句意为他整个冬天都穿同一件灰大衣，从不抱怨。被日日穿戴而磨损的袖口，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：穿、戴；磨损、用旧；耐用
名词：磨损；衣着（多用于复合词）

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转形容词，义为「磨破的；疲惫的」
加 -ing 构成形容词，义为「令人疲惫的」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「穿戴者」
加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可穿戴的（含电子设备）」

senses.title: To have clothes on
senses.titleCN: 穿、戴：把衣物首饰带在身上
senses.definition: to have clothes, shoes, glasses or jewellery on the body
senses.definitionCN: 把衣服、鞋、眼镜或首饰带在身上
senses.example: She wears glasses only when she reads.
senses.exampleCN: 她只在看书时戴眼镜。
senses.why: Old English werian meant to have on the body; the idea is carrying something on yourself, not putting it away.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 werian 意为「穿在身上」；这一观念是把东西带在身上，而不是收起来。

senses.title: To have a look or expression
senses.titleCN: 面带：带着某种神情或气色
senses.definition: to have a particular expression or appearance on the face
senses.definitionCN: 脸上带着某种表情或样子
senses.example: He wore a tired smile all through the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 整场会议他都带着疲惫的笑。
senses.why: The face is treated like clothing: an expression can be put on and carried about.
senses.whyCN: 脸被当作衣物来对待：表情也能穿上身，带着走来走去。

senses.title: To damage by use
senses.titleCN: 磨损：长期使用而变薄变坏
senses.definition: to damage or make thin by long or repeated use
senses.definitionCN: 因长期或反复使用而磨损、变薄
senses.example: The stairs were worn hollow in the middle.
senses.exampleCN: 那段楼梯中间被踏得凹了下去。
senses.why: Use rubs away material; the same verb now describes what the wearing does to the thing.
senses.whyCN: 使用会磨去材质；同一个动词此时描述这种穿戴对东西做了什么。

senses.title: To last in use
senses.definition: to remain in good condition after much use, used of materials and products
senses.definitionCN: 指材料与产品经久使用仍完好
senses.example: Good leather shoes wear well for years.
senses.exampleCN: 好皮鞋能穿好多年。
senses.why: The same process is viewed from the object's side: either it rubs away or it holds.
senses.whyCN: 同一过程从物体这一侧看：它或磨掉，或撑住。

senses.title: The damage itself
senses.definition: the damage or loss of material caused by use
senses.definitionCN: 因使用造成的材质损耗
senses.example: Check the tyres for wear before the long drive.
senses.exampleCN: 长途驾驶前检查轮胎的磨损。
senses.why: The action becomes a noun, and the noun names the mark left behind.
senses.whyCN: 动作化为名词，而名词指留下的痕迹。

intro.en: Wear is an Old English verb meaning to carry on the body, and it has always had both the clothing and the rubbing sense.
intro.cn: wear 是古英语动词，意为「在身上带着」，一直兼具穿戴与摩擦两个意思。

items.en: Werian meant 'to wear, to have on the body', and also 'to defend' in an older layer.
items.cn: werian 意为「穿、把……带在身上」，更早一层还有「防护」之义。

items.en: The past forms wore and worn keep an old vowel pattern shared with bear and swear.
items.cn: 过去式 wore 与过去分词 worn 保留了与 bear、swear 共有的古老元音模式。

items.en: A separate verb, often written werian as well, meant to weary or tire, and the 'wear out' sense grew partly from it.
items.cn: 另一个动词（也常写作 werian）意为使疲乏，wear out 的「耗尽」义部分源自它。

items.en: The clothing and the rubbing senses were already side by side, as they are today.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，穿戴义与磨损义已经并列，一如今天。

items.en: New compounds keep arriving: footwear, sportswear, wearable devices.
items.cn: 新的复合词不断出现：footwear、sportswear、wearable devices。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the wear family; the near-meaning group gathers dressing and damaging words.
note.cn: 形近组收 wear 一族词；近义组收穿衣与磨损类词。

entries.definition: Damaged by use, or very tired; the past participle as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「磨破的、疲惫的」，是过去分词转来的形容词。

entries.definition: Tiring to do or to be with.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人疲惫的」。

entries.definition: The person who has something on.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「穿戴者」。

entries.definition: The question word for place; a homophone trap.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在哪里」，与 wear 同音，易混。

entries.definition: To put clothes on; more about the act than about having them on.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「穿衣」，侧重穿衣动作。

entries.definition: To place clothes on the body at one moment; wear is the resulting state.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语，义为「穿上」，指某一刻的动作，而 wear 是穿着的状态。

entries.definition: To wear away slowly by natural forces such as water or wind.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「侵蚀」，多指自然力缓慢磨去。

entries.definition: Of cloth, to become worn into loose threads.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「磨散」，多指布料磨出线头。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English werian and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 werian，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Put on is the moment; wear is the day that follows.
normal.cn: put on 是那一刻；wear 是之后的一整天。

normal.en: Wear out means both used up and tired out.
normal.cn: wear out 既指磨坏，也指累垮。

normal.en: Wear off is for a feeling or a mark slowly leaving.
normal.cn: wear off 指感觉或痕迹慢慢消失。

normal.en: When patience wears thin, the same cloth image is at work.
normal.cn: 耐心 wearable thin 时，用的还是同一块布的形象。

normal.en: Wore and worn follow the pattern of bore, borne and tore, torn.
normal.cn: wore 与 worn 遵循 bore、borne、tore、torn 的模式。

abstract.en: Picture a coat cuff rolled up every morning: the cloth thins exactly where the habit happens.
abstract.cn: 想象每天早晨都挽起的袖口：布料正是在习惯发生的地方变薄。

abstract.en: Clothing and erosion are one word because both are things carried and rubbed by daily life.
abstract.cn: 穿衣与磨损是同一个词，因为两者都是被日常生活带着、磨着的东西。

abstract.en: A face can wear a smile for the same reason a body wears a coat: both are put on for others to see.
abstract.cn: 脸可以带着笑，正如身体穿着外套：两样都是穿给旁人看的。

examples.en: He wore a dark suit to the interview.
examples.cn: 他穿了深色西装去面试。

examples.en: The carpet has worn thin near the door.
examples.cn: 门口那块地毯已经磨薄了。

examples.en: This jacket has worn well for six winters.
examples.cn: 这件夹克已经穿了六个冬天，依然耐穿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂（wea）儿（r）」——每天喂孩子穿衣，衣服慢慢被穿旧：穿；磨损

root: 古英语 werian「穿、带在身上」，源自日耳曼语同一词根；过去式 wore、过去分词 worn 保留古老元音变换；同族词有 worn、wearer、wearable。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of wear run from clothes on the body, to a look worn on the face, to material rubbed away, to a thing that lasts, and finally to the damage itself.
sensesIntro.cn: wear 的五个义项从身上的衣物，到脸上的神情，到被磨去的材质，到经得起使用，最后是磨损本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coat cuff rolled up each morning, the cloth gone thin where the habit falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：每天早晨挽起的袖口，习惯落处布料变薄。

branches.en: BODY LINE: clothes and expressions are both carried on us.
branches.cn: 身体线：衣物与神情都是带在身上的。

branches.en: EROSION LINE: use rubs the material away.
branches.cn: 侵蚀线：使用把材质磨去。

branches.en: DURABILITY LINE: the same rubbing seen from the object's side.
branches.cn: 耐用线：同一摩擦从物体一侧来看。

branches.en: RESULT LINE: the noun names the mark left by use.
branches.cn: 结果线：名词指使用留下的痕迹。

branches.en: CONTRAST: put on is a moment, wear is a state.
branches.cn: 对照线：put on 是瞬间，wear 是状态。

intro.en: Wear is a strong native verb; its derivatives use plain English endings.
intro.cn: wear 是本族的强变化动词，其派生词使用普通英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

definition_zh: 硬的；坚固的；困难的；努力的；猛烈地；努力地
definition_en: firm and stiff to touch; difficult to do or understand; with great effort or force
core_image: 攥紧的拳头：握得越紧越用力，也越难被改变
scene: 他反复敲那张旧木桌，声音又闷又沉，木头结实得像石头。 He knocked on the old wooden desk again and again; the wood felt hard as stone.
sceneCN: 这里 hard 是「硬的、坚固的」（第 1 个义项：质地坚硬不易变形）；木头结实得像石头，说明它摸起来硬、不易弯曲，属于 hard 最基本的触感义。

derivatives.zh: 使变硬；变硬，由 hard 加动词后缀 -en 构成，表示「变得坚硬」
硬度；坚硬，由 hard 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，指坚硬的性质
几乎不；简直不，由 hard 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，语义弱化为否定

senses.title: Firm and stiff
senses.definition: not soft and difficult to bend, break, or press
senses.definitionCN: 不软，难以弯曲、折断或压扁
senses.example: The ground was hard after weeks without rain.
senses.exampleCN: 几个星期没下雨，地面变硬了。
senses.why: The core image is a clenched fist: something pressed tight resists change, so the physical sense of firmness comes first.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是攥紧的拳头：被压紧的东西抗拒改变，所以「质地坚硬」成为最直接的身体感受，也是最早的义项。

senses.title: Difficult to do
senses.definition: difficult to do, understand, or answer
senses.definitionCN: 难做、难懂或难回答
senses.example: That was a hard question on the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 那是考试里一道很难的题。
senses.why: When something resists your effort the way stone resists your hand, the feeling of resistance extends to tasks, so hard comes to mean difficult.
senses.whyCN: 当一件事像石头挡住手一样挡住你的努力时，这种「阻力感」就从触感转移到任务上，于是 hard 引申出「困难」义。

senses.title: With great effort
senses.definition: using a lot of effort or energy
senses.definitionCN: 付出大量力气或精力去做
senses.example: She worked hard to finish the project on time.
senses.exampleCN: 她努力工作，按时完成了项目。
senses.why: Doing something difficult requires pushing with force, so the adjective of resistance becomes an adverb of intense effort.
senses.whyCN: 做困难的事需要用大力气去推，表示「有阻力」的形容词由此变成表示「用力、努力」的副词。

senses.title: Severe or harsh
senses.definition: not kind or gentle; treating people in a severe way
senses.definitionCN: 不温和，对待人严厉苛刻
senses.example: The teacher was hard on students who came late.
senses.exampleCN: 老师对迟到的学生很严厉。
senses.why: A surface that gives no comfort feels cold and unyielding, so hard extends to attitudes that give no mercy or gentleness.
senses.whyCN: 不给人舒服余地的表面冷硬不弯，这种感受延伸到人的态度上，就有了「严厉、苛刻」义。

intro.en: Hard is one of the oldest English adjectives, tracing straight back to Germanic roots.
intro.cn: hard 是英语最古老的形容词之一，可以直接追溯到日耳曼语词根。

items.en: Old English had heard, meaning solid and firm, already covering both physical hardness and difficulty.
items.cn: 古英语作 heard，意为「坚固的」，已经同时覆盖「坚硬」和「困难」两个意思。

items.en: It comes from the reconstructed Germanic root *harðuz, shared across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 它来自重构的日耳曼词根 *harðuz，在各日耳曼语言中广泛共用。

items.en: Old Norse harðr, meaning hard and severe, is a close relative that reinforced the English word.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 harðr 意为「坚硬、严厉」，是英语这个词的近亲，强化了它的用法。

items.en: German hart keeps the same meaning today, showing how stable this root has been.
items.cn: 德语 hart 至今意义相同，可见这个词根非常稳定。

items.en: In Modern English, hard split into the adjectival and adverbial uses, while hardly drifted to mean almost not.
items.cn: 现代英语里，hard 分出形容词与副词用法，而 hardly 则漂移为「几乎不」的意思。

note.en: Words that share the shape or the meaning field of hard.
note.cn: 与 hard 形近或义近的词。

entries.definition: to become or make something hard
entries.definitionCN: 使变硬；硬化，与 hard 同根，加动词后缀 -en

entries.definition: severe suffering or difficulty
entries.definitionCN: 艰难；困苦，同根词，指生活上的艰苦

entries.definition: metal tools and the physical parts of a computer
entries.definitionCN: 五金器具；计算机硬件，hard 与 ware 的合成词

entries.definition: not easy to do or understand
entries.definitionCN: 困难的；不易的，义场相近但词源不同

entries.definition: solid and not likely to change
entries.definitionCN: 坚固的；坚定的，与 hard 第一个义项相近

entries.definition: strong and difficult to break or chew
entries.definitionCN: 坚韧的；难对付的，与 hard 义场重叠

normalIntro.en: Five routes into the word hard.
normalIntro.cn: 五条记住 hard 的路径。

normal.en: hard and hardness
normal.cn: hard 与 hardness：hard 是「硬」，hardness 是「硬度」，同根好记。

normal.en: hard as stone
normal.cn: 短语「hard as stone」（硬得像石头）把触感义锁进画面。

normal.en: hard question
normal.cn: 短语「hard question」（难题）把困难义固定下来。

normal.en: work hard
normal.cn: 搭配「work hard」（努力工作）锁定副词用法。

normal.en: hardly the opposite
normal.cn: hardly 已经漂移成「几乎不」，别把它当成 hard 的普通副词形式。

abstract.en: Picture a fist clenched so tight that nothing can bend it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只攥得死紧的拳头，什么都掰不动它——这就是 hard 的核心画面。

abstract.en: Feel a stone wall refusing your push.
abstract.cn: 感受一堵石墙拒绝你推过去的手掌：阻力感就是 hard 的全部含义。

abstract.en: Link the resistance of stone to the resistance of a task.
abstract.cn: 把石头的阻力接到任务的阻力上：硬的东西难推动，难的事 hard to do。

examples.en: The bread had gone hard after two days in the open air.
examples.cn: 面包在露天放了两天，已经变硬了。

examples.en: It is hard to keep a secret when everyone is asking questions.
examples.cn: 当所有人都在追问时，保守秘密很难。

examples.en: He trains hard every morning before school.
examples.cn: 他每天早晨上学前都刻苦训练。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈的」——敲桌子敲得「哈」一声，因为桌面是硬的；硬的东西难推，难的事要努力干。

root: hard 来自原始日耳曼语词根 *harðuz（坚硬），古英语作 heard。这个词根在日耳曼语系中高度稳定，德语 hart 与之同源。词义从「质地坚硬」自然引申为「困难」「用力」「严厉」，属于典型的触感隐喻扩展。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from physical firmness to difficulty, effort, and severity.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从身体的坚硬感出发，延伸到困难、用力与严厉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clenched fist that nothing can bend
core.cn: 核心意象：攥紧的拳头，什么都掰不动

branches.en: Solid things that resist touch
branches.cn: 坚硬抵抗触碰的物体

branches.en: Tasks that resist effort
branches.cn: 抵抗努力的困难任务

branches.en: Actions done with force
branches.cn: 用力做出的行为

branches.en: Attitudes that give no comfort
branches.cn: 不留情面的严厉态度

branches.en: One resistance, two worlds
branches.cn: 同一种阻力感，分出触感与任务两界

intro.en: Hard forms a small but productive Germanic family.
intro.cn: hard 构成一个规模不大但能产的日耳曼词族。

latinIntro.en: Hard is Germanic, so there are no Latin relatives here.
latinIntro.cn: hard 属日耳曼词源，没有拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 魔法；巫术；魔术；戏法；魔力；魅力；神奇的；迷人的
definition_en: supposed supernatural power over events, the tricks of a stage performer, a compelling charm, or, as an adjective, wonderful and enchanting
core_image: 一顶高礼帽、一根细棒，白鸽从空空的袖口里扑棱飞出来
scene: 后台的道具箱里放着假鸽子、彩带和一顶高礼帽，幕布只拉开一半。 The audience applauded as the magic began in a puff of smoke.
sceneCN: 这里 magic 是「魔术、戏法」（第 2 个义项：舞台上的障眼技艺）；句意为观众在一阵烟雾中迎来魔术开场，随即鼓起掌来。图中可辨识物件：高礼帽、彩带、半开的幕布。

pos.zh: 魔法；巫术；魔术；戏法；魔力；魅力
神奇的；有魔力的；迷人的

collocations.zh: 效果奇佳；像施了魔法一样

derivatives.zh: 由 magic 加 -al 构成，义为「魔法的；迷人的」
由 magic 加 -ian 构成，义为「魔术师；巫师」
由 magical 加 -ly 构成，义为「靠魔法地；神奇地」

senses.title: Supernatural power used to change events
senses.definition: the supposed power to make things happen by charms, spells or secret forces beyond nature
senses.definitionCN: 通过咒语、符咒或超自然隐秘力量左右事物的、被认为存在的能力
senses.example: The villagers believed that a curse could be lifted by magic.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们相信那道咒语可以靠魔法解除。
senses.why: Greek magos named a Persian priest who read the stars, and the craft of such a priest became the ordinary word for power over events that nature does not explain.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 magos 指波斯的占星祭司，这类祭司的技艺后来成了「支配自然无法解释之事的力量」的日常说法。

senses.title: Conjuring tricks performed on stage
senses.definition: the art of producing baffling effects by sleight of hand, hidden props and misdirection
senses.definitionCN: 依靠手上功夫、暗藏道具与转移注意，制造出令人困惑效果的行当
senses.example: Her act mixed quick card magic with a dove that vanished from a hat.
senses.exampleCN: 她的节目把快速的纸牌魔术和一只从帽子里消失的鸽子混在一起。
senses.why: A stage performer copies the effects the old craft claimed, so the same noun now names a trick that everyone knows is a trick.
senses.whyCN: 舞台艺人复制了古老技艺号称能做到的效果，于是同一个名词如今指一场人人都知道是假的戏法。

senses.title: A compelling, unexplained charm
senses.definition: a quality in a place, person or moment that seems to work on people beyond ordinary cause
senses.definitionCN: 某地、某人或某一刻身上那种仿佛超出常理、能打动人的特质
senses.example: There is a certain magic in the old market at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时分的旧集市有一种说不清的魔力。
senses.why: If magic means power that acts without visible cause, then a place that moves people without explanation can simply be said to have magic in it.
senses.whyCN: 如果 magic 指没有可见原因就起作用的力量，那么一个说不清为何打动人的地方，自然就可以说身上带着魔力。

senses.title: Wonderful and enchanting, as an adjective
senses.definition: used beside a noun for something that seems to work beyond ordinary means or feels enchanting
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词旁边，形容某物仿佛以超乎常理的方式奏效，或令人觉得着迷
senses.example: The garden looked magic under the first snow of winter.
senses.exampleCN: 初雪落下时，那座园子看起来像被施了魔法。
senses.why: Once the noun names a power that changes things, placing it beside another noun turns it into a plain adjective for the effect.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个名词指一种改变事物的力量，把它放到另一个名词旁边，就自然变成了描述那种效果的形容词。

intro.en: Magic is a word borrowed from the title of a foreign priesthood; it then split into a claimed supernatural art, a harmless stage act, a felt charm and a plain adjective.
intro.cn: magic 是从一个外来祭司称号借来的词；它后来分成号称的超自然技艺、人畜无害的舞台戏法、可感觉得到的魅力，以及一个普通形容词。

items.en: The word is generally traced to Old Persian maguš, a member of a priestly class who read the stars and performed rites.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词可追到古波斯语 maguš，指主持仪式、观测星象的祭司阶层成员。

items.en: Greek adopted the title as magos for a Persian priest or a wandering wise man, and the abstract craft was called magikē.
items.cn: 希腊语把这个称号借作 magos，指波斯祭司或游走的智者，而那种抽象的技艺被称为 magikē。

items.en: Latin took the Greek adjective as magicus, and the related noun named the art itself rather than the man.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个希腊形容词借作 magicus，相关的名词则指那门技艺本身，而不是那个人。

items.en: Old French magique carried noun and adjective into medieval Europe, and English borrowed the forms in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries.
items.cn: 古法语 magique 把名词与形容词一起带进中世纪的欧洲，英语在十三、十四世纪借入这些形式。

items.en: Modern English keeps magic for the occult art and for the stage act, adds the figurative charm, and uses the bare noun before other nouns as an adjective.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 magic 指神秘技艺与舞台表演，加上比喻性的魅力，并把光秃秃的名词放在其他名词前当形容词用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivatives and the biblical plural of the priestly title; the near group gathers other words for magic arts and for tricks of the senses.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词与那个祭司称号的圣经复数；近义组收其他表示法术以及感官幻象的词。

entries.definition: Relating to magic, or enchanting.
entries.definitionCN: 与魔法有关的；迷人的；由 magic 加 -al 构成。

entries.definition: A person who performs magic or conjuring tricks.
entries.definitionCN: 施行魔法的人或魔术师；由 magic 加 -ian 构成。

entries.definition: By magic, or in a way that seems magical.
entries.definitionCN: 靠魔法地；像魔法般神奇地；由 magical 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The wise men from the East in the Christmas story, from Greek magos.
entries.definitionCN: 圣诞故事中来自东方的贤士；出自希腊语 magos，与 magic 同源。

entries.definition: Magic performed with the help of spirits or demons.
entries.definitionCN: 借助精灵或魔鬼施行的法术。

entries.definition: The practice of magic, especially with a claimed pact with evil powers.
entries.definitionCN: 行施法术，尤指号称与邪恶力量立约的做法。

entries.definition: A false impression created by a trick of the eye or of the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 由眼睛或心理的花招造成的错误印象。

entries.definition: A set of words believed to have magical power.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为带有魔力的一组词语。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as the title of a foreign priest, and its family keeps returning to hidden knowledge, stage deception and the charm that needs no explanation.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起初是一个外来祭司的称号，它的同族词反复回到隐秘的知识、舞台上的障眼法，以及无需解释的魅力。

normal.en: Greek magos came from Old Persian maguš, a priest who read the stars, and the craft of such a priest became magikē in Greek.
normal.cn: 希腊语 magos 出自古波斯语 maguš，指观星的祭司；这类祭司的技艺在希腊语里成了 magikē。

normal.en: Latin magicus and Old French magique carried the word to English, which shortened the ending to magic.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 magicus 与古法语 magique 把词带到英语，英语把词尾缩短成 magic。

normal.en: Magician adds -ian to name the person, magical adds -al for the quality, and magically adds -ly for the manner.
normal.cn: magician 加 -ian 指人，magical 加 -al 指性质，magically 再加 -ly 指方式。

normal.en: A magic wand and a magic trick keep the stage sense, while black magic keeps the darker ritual sense.
normal.cn: magic wand 与 magic trick 守住舞台义，black magic 守住了更阴暗的仪式义。

normal.en: The adjective use grew by putting the noun before another noun, as in a magic spell or a magic touch.
normal.cn: 形容词用法是把名词放到另一个名词前长出来的，如 a magic spell、a magic touch。

abstract.en: A word borrowed from a foreign priesthood now names both a stage trick and a real feeling of enchantment.
abstract.cn: 一个从外来祭司制度借来的词，如今既指舞台戏法，也指真实可感的着迷。

abstract.en: Magic survives because people still want a short name for effects they cannot explain.
abstract.cn: magic 之所以还在用，是因为人仍然需要一个短词来称呼自己解释不了的效果。

abstract.en: The same word covers a trick you can learn and a power you can only imagine.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指可以学会的戏法，也指只能想象的力量。

examples.en: The audience applauded as the magic began in a puff of smoke.
examples.cn: 观众在一阵烟雾中迎来魔术开场，随即鼓起掌来。

examples.en: The villagers believed that a curse could be lifted by magic.
examples.cn: 村民们相信那道咒语可以靠魔法解除。

examples.en: There is a certain magic in the old market at dusk.
examples.cn: 黄昏时分的旧集市有一种说不清的魔力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马吉克」——马戏团里的吉克一挥手就变出鸽子；记住 magic 是魔术，也是魔法。

root: 希腊语 magos（波斯的祭司、占星师）→ 希腊语 magikē（祭司的技艺）→ 拉丁语 magicus → 古法语 magique → 英语 magic；一般认为可追到古波斯语 maguš。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a power that acts without visible cause; the senses then divide into the claimed occult art, the stage trick that copies it, a felt charm and an everyday adjective.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一种没有可见原因就起作用的力量；义项由此分成号称的神秘技艺、复制它的舞台戏法、可感觉得到的魅力，以及日常形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tall hat, a thin wand, and a white dove bursting out of an empty sleeve.
core.cn: 核心意象：一顶高礼帽、一根细棒，白鸽从空空的袖口里扑棱飞出。

branches.en: a stargazer reading a chart by lamplight
branches.cn: 占星者在灯下读星图

branches.en: a hand passing over a bowl of water
branches.cn: 一只手从水碗上方掠过

branches.en: a white dove flapping out of an empty hat
branches.cn: 白鸽从空帽子里拍翅飞出

branches.en: lanterns coming on above an old square
branches.cn: 老广场上方灯笼次第亮起

branches.en: snow settling on a silent garden
branches.cn: 雪落在寂静的园子里

intro.en: A Persian priestly title, its Greek and Latin forms, one French borrowing and three English endings carry magic from a foreign caste to the stage and to a feeling in a place.
intro.cn: 一个波斯的祭司称号、它的希腊语与拉丁语形式、一次法语借入，再加三个英语词尾，把 magic 从外来的祭司阶层带到舞台与一个地方的氛围。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms magicus and magus are recorded, and both descend from Greek magos, which in turn is generally traced to Old Persian maguš.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形式 magicus 与 magus 均有记录，二者都出自希腊语 magos，而后者一般认为可追到古波斯语 maguš。

latinEntries.meaning: a magus, a wise man from the East

definition_zh: 然后；当时；那么；（紧接）于是；那时以来的
definition_en: at that time; next in order or consequence; or in that case, following from what has been said
core_image: 时间线上的下一格：上一个事件落定，指针才拨到它
scene: 烤箱计时器响了，她放下书起身。 Beat the eggs, then fold in the flour gently.
sceneCN: 这里 then 是「然后」（第 1 个义项：紧接的下一时间）；句意：打散鸡蛋，然后轻轻拌入面粉。

collocations.zh: 不过话说回来；转念一想

derivatives.zh: 比（then 的孪生词，同出古英语一词后分化）
当场；立即（固定短语）
之后（同义时间副词，更书面）

senses.title: Next in time or order
senses.definition: at the next moment in a sequence of actions or events
senses.definitionCN: 在一系列动作或事件中的下一时刻
senses.example: Wash the rice, then soak it for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 淘米，然后浸泡一小时。
senses.why: The timeline has slots; then fills the one right after the last filled slot.
senses.whyCN: 时间线上有格子；then 填入紧随上一个已填格子的那一格。

senses.title: At a past or future time
senses.definition: at a particular time referred to in the past or future
senses.definitionCN: 在过去或未来所指的某个时间
senses.example: By then the sun had already set.
senses.exampleCN: 到那时太阳已经落山。
senses.why: Then can park at any single point on the line, not only the next one.
senses.whyCN: then 可以停在线上的任意一点，而不只是下一格。

senses.title: In that case; as a consequence
senses.definition: following logically from what has just been said, as in if you need help, then ask
senses.definitionCN: 从刚说的话逻辑地推出，如 if you need help, then ask
senses.example: If the last bus has gone, then we walk.
senses.exampleCN: 如果末班车已走，那我们就走路。
senses.why: The time pointer is bent into logic: when the condition is set, its result is the next slot.
senses.whyCN: 时间指针被弯成逻辑：条件一旦成立，结果便是下一格。

senses.title: Being so at the time mentioned
senses.definition: used before a title to mean holding it at that time, as in the then president
senses.definitionCN: 用于头衔前，表示当时任此职，如 the then president
senses.example: The then mayor opened the bridge in nineteen thirty.
senses.exampleCN: 时任市长于一九三零年为大桥剪彩。
senses.why: The adverb leans against a noun to date-stamp it.
senses.whyCN: 副词斜倚名词，为其盖上日期戳。

intro.en: Then is the older spelling of a word that split in two: the Old English adverb þanne meant both at that time and than. Modern English kept both senses but gave each a spelling.
intro.cn: then 是一个一分为二的词的旧拼写：古英语副词 þanne 既指「那时」也作「比」。现代英语保留两个义项，但各配一个拼写。

items.en: Þanne, also written þonne, meant at that time and served comparison alike.
items.cn: þanne（亦作 þonne）意为那时，同样充当比较词。

items.en: It descends from a Germanic demonstrative adverb related to that, a pointer aimed at time.
items.cn: 它源自日耳曼指示副词，与 that 相关，是瞄准时间的指针。

items.en: Middle English spelled it then, than, panne; time and comparison senses interchanged freely.
items.cn: 中古英语拼作 then、than、panne；时间义与比较义自由互换。

items.en: The correlative use the earlier ... then the later prepared the logical sense.
items.cn: 「先……then 后……」的呼应用法为逻辑义作了铺垫。

items.en: By the seventeenth century then kept time and logic, while than was reserved for comparison.
items.cn: 至十七世纪，then 保留时间与逻辑义，than 专管比较。

note.en: The first group is the twin and its family; the second lines up the time words that share the timeline.
note.cn: 第一组是孪生词及其家族；第二组排列共享时间线的词。

entries.definition: the comparison twin; one word in Old English, two spellings now
entries.definitionCN: 比较孪生词；古英语原是一词，如今两副拼写

entries.definition: the object pronoun; one letter apart in writing
entries.definitionCN: 宾格代词；书写上只差一字母

entries.definition: the topic word; looks close, unrelated
entries.definitionCN: 主题词；形近而源异

entries.definition: later, without the tight next-slot feel of then
entries.definitionCN: 之后；没有 then 紧贴下一格之感

entries.definition: the other consequence word; so states the result, then delivers it
entries.definitionCN: 另一个表结果的词；so 宣布结果，then 交付结果

entries.definition: the next item in order, usually without a clock behind it
entries.definitionCN: 下一项；通常背后无钟表

normalIntro.en: Real links: the twin than, the Old English pointer, if-then logic, and the then president.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：孪生词 than、古英语指针、if-then 逻辑、以及 the then president。

normal.en: Then and than were one word until spelling split them.
normal.cn: then 与 than 本是一词，拼写才分了家。

normal.en: First the eggs, then the flour: slots on a timeline.
normal.cn: 先鸡蛋，后面粉：时间线上的格子。

normal.en: If A, then B: time logic made visible.
normal.cn: if A, then B：把时间逻辑显形。

normal.en: The then mayor: a date stamp pressed onto a title.
normal.cn: the then mayor：盖在头衔上的日期戳。

normal.en: Now and then: two ends of the same pointer.
normal.cn: now and then：同一指针的两端。

abstract.en: Sequencing is the first logic a child learns, and then is its grammar.
abstract.cn: 排序是儿童学到的第一种逻辑，then 是它的语法。

abstract.en: A consequence is just a future that a condition has already chosen.
abstract.cn: 结果不过是条件早已选定的未来。

abstract.en: One old pointer split into time, logic and comparison.
abstract.cn: 一根古老的指针分成了时间、逻辑与比较。

examples.en: She signed the form, then left without a word.
examples.cn: 她签了字，然后一言不发地离开。

examples.en: Back then, nobody owned more than one phone.
examples.cn: 那时候，没有人有超过一部手机。

examples.en: If the rain stops, then the match starts at three.
examples.cn: 如果雨停，比赛三点开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赞」——上一件事刚做完就「赞」到下一件，接得快 → then 然后

root: 古英语副词 þanne/þonne（那时；亦作比较词）→ 日耳曼指示副词 → 近代英语与 than 拼写分化，then 保留时间与逻辑义。

sensesIntro.en: Then starts as a pointer at the next moment, can rest at any single time, bends into logical consequence, and finally leans on titles as a date stamp.
sensesIntro.cn: then 起于指向下一刻的指针，可停驻任意时点，弯成逻辑推论，最终斜倚头衔作日期戳。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the clock hand clicking to the next notch.
core.cn: 核心意象：钟表指针咔哒一声拨到下一格。

branches.en: The next slot on the timeline.
branches.cn: 时间线上的下一格。

branches.en: Parked at any chosen moment.
branches.cn: 停驻于任一选定时刻。

branches.en: The pointer bent into if-then logic.
branches.cn: 被弯成 if-then 逻辑的指针。

branches.en: The pointer pressed flat onto a title.
branches.cn: 被压平贴上头衔的指针。

branches.en: Sequence and consequence share one clicking hand.
branches.cn: 排序与推论共用同一只咔哒之手。

intro.en: Then has no affixes; its family is the split twin than and the demonstrative ancestors.
intro.cn: then 没有词缀；其家族是孪生词 than 及指示词祖先。

latinIntro.en: Then is Germanic; the Latin time adverbs are given only as contrast.
latinIntro.cn: then 属日耳曼语源；拉丁时间副词仅作对照。

items.meaning: then; the single ancestor of then and than
items.meaningCN: then 与 than 的共同祖先
items.example: Þanne split into then and than.
items.exampleCN: þanne 分成了 then 与 than。

items.example: By then the shops had shut.
Maybe not, then again maybe yes.

definition_zh: 上升；站起；增长；起源
definition_en: to move upward, stand up, or increase; also the act of rising
core_image: 海面上缓缓升起的太阳
scene: 太阳从海面上升起，渔船陆续出海。 The sun rose over the sea and the boats set out.
sceneCN: 这里 rise 是「升起」（第 1 个义项：向上移动）；句意：太阳从海面上升起，渔船陆续出海。

derivatives.zh: 上升的；增长的
升起的；复活的
早起者；竖板

senses.title: Moving upward
senses.definition: to move from a lower place to a higher one
senses.definitionCN: 从较低处移到较高处
senses.example: Smoke rose from the chimney.
senses.exampleCN: 烟从烟囱里升起。
senses.why: The core act is simple upward movement.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作就是单纯的向上移动。

senses.title: Standing up
senses.definition: to get up from sitting or lying
senses.definitionCN: 从坐卧状态起身
senses.example: Everyone rose when the judge entered.
senses.exampleCN: 法官进来时大家都站了起来。
senses.why: Standing lifts the body upward.
senses.whyCN: 站立就是把身体向上抬起。

senses.title: An increase
senses.definition: an increase in amount or level
senses.definitionCN: 数量或水平的增加
senses.example: There was a sharp rise in prices.
senses.exampleCN: 物价急剧上涨。
senses.why: A number that goes up is also rising.
senses.whyCN: 数字向上走也是上升。

senses.title: A beginning
senses.definition: the start or cause of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的开端或原因
senses.example: The quarrel gave rise to a long feud.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争吵引发了长期的仇怨。
senses.why: Things rise from a source, as smoke from fire.
senses.whyCN: 事物从源头升起，就像烟从火起。

intro.en: Rise comes from Old English rīsan, to rise or get up.
intro.cn: rise 源自古英语 rīsan，意为升起或起身。

items.en: Rīsan means to rise.
items.cn: rīsan 意为升起。

items.en: The sun and smoke both rise.
items.cn: 太阳与烟都会升起。

items.en: Prices begin to rise in trade talk.
items.cn: 贸易语境中价格开始上涨。

items.en: Give rise to means cause.
items.cn: give rise to 意为引起。

items.en: Rise stays irregular: rise, rose, risen.
items.cn: rise 保持不规则变化：rise、rose、risen。

note.en: Rise does not take an object; raise needs one.
note.cn: rise 不带宾语，raise 需要带宾语。

entries.definition: having gone up
entries.definitionCN: 已升起

entries.definition: going up
entries.definitionCN: 正在上升

entries.definition: to happen or appear
entries.definitionCN: 出现；发生

entries.definition: to go up with effort
entries.definitionCN: 攀登

entries.definition: to become larger
entries.definitionCN: 增加

entries.definition: to be on your feet
entries.definitionCN: 站立

normalIntro.en: Rise is the upward line of smoke or sun.
normalIntro.cn: rise 就是烟或太阳向上的那条线。

normal.en: The sun rises in the east.
normal.cn: the sun rises 太阳从东方升起。

normal.en: Rise up means get up or fight back.
normal.cn: rise up 意为起身或反抗。

normal.en: A sharp rise means a fast increase.
normal.cn: a sharp rise 意为快速上涨。

normal.en: Give rise to means cause something.
normal.cn: give rise to 意为引起某事。

normal.en: Rise above means go beyond a problem.
normal.cn: rise above 意为超越问题。

abstract.en: Picture a red sun lifting off the water.
abstract.cn: 想象一轮红日从水面升起。

abstract.en: Imagine smoke curling up a cold chimney.
abstract.cn: 想象烟从冰冷的烟囱里卷上去。

abstract.en: Think of a graph line climbing to the right.
abstract.cn: 想象一条折线向右上方攀升。

examples.en: Prices rose by ten percent last year.
examples.cn: 去年物价上涨了百分之十。

examples.en: She rose to answer the question.
examples.cn: 她站起来回答问题。

examples.en: The plan gave rise to many doubts.
examples.cn: 这个计划引起了诸多疑虑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rise」听起来像「拉起」——被拉起来，就是上升。

root: 古英语 rīsan（升起）→ rise，核心义「自下而上移动」，从太阳、身体到物价与起因都能延伸。

sensesIntro.en: Rise means to go up, to stand, to increase, or to begin from a source.
sensesIntro.cn: rise 意为向上、起身、增长，或从某处起源。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an upward line against the sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：天空下一条向上的线。

branches.en: Simple upward movement is the core.
branches.cn: 单纯的向上移动是核心。

branches.en: Standing raises the body from a chair.
branches.cn: 站起是把身体从椅子上抬起。

branches.en: Numbers that grow follow the same line.
branches.cn: 增长的数字沿着同样的线。

branches.en: A source sends things upward like smoke.
branches.cn: 源头把事物像烟一样向上送出。

branches.en: Physical and numeric rising share one image.
branches.cn: 物理上升与数字上涨共享同一个意象。

intro.en: Rise is a native irregular verb from Old English rīsan.
intro.cn: rise 是源自古英语 rīsan 的英语本族不规则动词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; ar- in arise is its closest prefix.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属于日耳曼语，arise 中的 ar- 是它最接近的前缀。

items.exampleCN: arise 是 rise 加 a-。

definition_zh: 产品；产物；成果；（数学）乘积；（化学）生成物
definition_en: something produced by a process, a reaction, a multiplication or human work
core_image: 流水线尽头，一只刚成型的物件被机械臂放进托盘，旁边堆着已经空了的料箱
scene: 流水线尽头，一只刚成型的物件被机械臂放进托盘，旁边堆着已经空了的料箱。 Water is the product of the reaction between hydrogen and oxygen.
sceneCN: 这里 product 指化学反应生成的产物（第 1 个义项：反应结束后新生成的物质）；句意：水是氢与氧反应的生成物。图中可辨识物件：传送带、机械臂、托盘、空料箱；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 产品；产物；成果；乘积；生成物

forms.label: 形容词（多产的；生产性的）

derivatives.zh: 生产；农产品
生产；产量；制作
多产的；富有成效的
生产率
生产者；制片人

senses.title: What a chemical reaction makes
senses.titleCN: 化学反应生成的新物质
senses.definition: a substance formed when other substances react
senses.definitionCN: 由其他物质发生反应后生成的新物质
senses.example: Water is the product of the reaction between hydrogen and oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 水是氢与氧反应的生成物。
senses.why: the word is the past participle of a Latin verb meaning to lead forth, so a product is literally what has been brought out of a process.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是拉丁动词「引出」的过去分词，因此 product 字面就是「被过程带出来的东西」。

senses.title: A thing made for sale
senses.definition: an item manufactured or grown in order to be sold
senses.definitionCN: 为出售而制造或种植的物品
senses.example: The company moved its best product to the front of the catalogue.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把最好的产品移到目录前页。
senses.why: commerce narrowed the general sense of what is brought forth to what is brought forth for a buyer.
senses.whyCN: 商业把「被带出来的东西」这一通义收窄为「为买家带出来的东西」。

senses.title: A result of effort
senses.definition: an outcome of work, thinking or events, often abstract
senses.definitionCN: 工作、思考或事件带来的结果，常为抽象之物
senses.example: The report was the product of three years of fieldwork.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告是三年野外工作的成果。
senses.why: if a process brings something out, anything brought out counts, including knowledge and institutions.
senses.whyCN: 只要过程能带出东西，被带出的一切都算，包括知识与制度。

senses.title: The result of multiplication
senses.definition: the number obtained by multiplying two or more numbers
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个数相乘所得的数
senses.example: The product of six and seven is forty-two.
senses.exampleCN: 六与七的乘积是四十二。
senses.why: mathematics borrowed the same participle: multiplication brings forth a number from two others.
senses.whyCN: 数学借用了同一个分词：乘法从两个数里带出一个数。

senses.title: A child of its time or place
senses.definition: a person or thing shaped entirely by a particular background
senses.definitionCN: 完全由某一背景塑造的人或事物
senses.example: He was a product of the same crowded schools he later criticized.
senses.exampleCN: 他正是他后来批评的那种拥挤学校的产物。
senses.why: the metaphor says that circumstances manufacture people in the way a factory manufactures goods.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻说环境造人，正如工厂造货。

senses.title: Farm output
senses.definition: crops or other goods grown from the land, often in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 地里种出的作物等物产，常用复数
senses.example: The market sells local products from the surrounding farms.
senses.exampleCN: 这个市场出售周边农场的本地农产品。
senses.why: farming speaks of its output as produce, and the plural products marks things grown rather than made.
senses.whyCN: 农业把自己的产出说成 produce，复数 products 标记的是种出来的东西，而非造出来的。

senses.title: A work of media or art
senses.titleCN: 媒体或艺术作品的产物
senses.definition: a film, recording or other creative work considered as an item made by a studio
senses.definitionCN: 被视为由制片机构制作的电影、录音等创作成品
senses.example: The studio treats every film as a product with a release date.
senses.exampleCN: 制片方把每部电影都当作有发行日期的产品。
senses.why: the entertainment industry uses the commercial sense of the word, so a film becomes a product beside toys and tickets.
senses.whyCN: 娱乐业使用这个词的商业义，于是电影与玩具、门票并列成为产品。

senses.title: One item in a brand range
senses.titleCN: 品牌系列中的单个品项
senses.definition: a single item within a company's range, tracked separately in sales and marketing
senses.definitionCN: 公司系列中的单个品项，在销售与营销中单独核算
senses.example: Each product in the range has its own price and its own page.
senses.exampleCN: 系列中的每个产品都有自己的价格与页面。
senses.why: marketing splits a range into countable units, and the word becomes the unit of accounting rather than the whole output.
senses.whyCN: 营销把一个系列拆成可数的单位，这个词于是成为核算单位，而不是全部产出。

intro.en: Product comes from Latin productum, the neuter past participle of producere, to lead forth, built on pro-, forward, and ducere, to lead. It entered English in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: product 出自拉丁语 productum，即 producere「引出」的中性过去分词；该动词由 pro-「向前」与 ducere「引导」构成。它在 16 世纪进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ducere meant to lead, draw or guide; its past participle ductum supplied a long series of English words. The deeper Indo-European root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导、拉、带领」，其过去分词 ductum 提供了一长串英语词。更早的印欧词根属于重构。

items.en: Pro-, forward, plus ducere produced producere, to lead forth, bring out, extend, which is the source of produce, product and production.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 ducere 构成 producere「引出、带出、延长」，是 produce、product 与 production 的来源。

items.en: The neuter participle productum came to be used as a noun for something brought out or brought forth, the direct model of the English word.
items.cn: 中性分词 productum 被当作名词使用，指被带出、被产生的东西，是英语词的直接样板。

items.en: Product entered English in the sixteenth century, first as a general word for a result and also as the mathematical term for the result of multiplication.
items.cn: product 于 16 世纪进入英语，最初泛指结果，同时也是表示乘法结果的数学术语。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the commercial sense of a manufactured item for sale became dominant, and the plural products spread into farming and marketing.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，指供出售的制成品这一商业义占据主导，复数形式 products 又扩散到农业与营销。

items.en: First date uncertain: the century of entry is well attested, but the earliest citation of the commercial sense is not settled, so the date given for that sense is approximate.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：进入英语的世纪有可靠记载，但商业义的最早书证尚无定论，因此为该义给出的年代只是约数。

note.en: The first group shares the produce stem; the second group names other results and other stages of making something.
note.cn: 第一组共享 produce 词干；第二组是其他表示结果或制作阶段的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to bring forth; its noun form, pronounced differently, means fresh farm goods as a mass.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「产生、生产」的动词；其名词形式读音不同，指作为整体的新鲜农产品。

entries.definition: The activity or amount of making things; a product is the thing, production is the making of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指制作活动或产量；product 是物，production 是制作这件事。

entries.definition: Something made incidentally while the main product is being made; it is not the intended output.
entries.definitionCN: 在制造主要产品时顺带产生的东西，不是有意要的产出。

entries.definition: The person or firm that makes the product; the -er ending marks the maker rather than the made.
entries.definitionCN: 制作产品的人或公司；词尾 -er 标记制作者，而不是被制作之物。

entries.definition: The general word for what follows from something; it does not imply that the thing was made or sold.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指由某事带来的结果；不含「被制造或被出售」的意思。

entries.definition: What a system turns out, often measured as a rate or total; it stresses quantity more than the item itself.
entries.definitionCN: 系统产出的东西，常以速率或总量计量；强调数量多过单件物品。

entries.definition: The amount obtained from a process, especially a reaction or a field; chemistry counts yield, not products alone.
entries.definitionCN: 从过程得到的量，尤指反应或田地；化学算的是收率，而不只是产物本身。

entries.definition: Movable items for sale, always plural; it is a commercial collective, while product can name one item.
entries.definitionCN: 可供出售的动产，总用复数；它是商业集合名词，而 product 可以指单件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb, the real word family and real commercial phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的同族词与真实的商业说法。

normal.en: Pro- forward plus ducere to lead: to lead something out of a process.
normal.cn: pro-「向前」加 ducere「引导」：把某物从过程中引出来。

normal.en: The family runs produce, product, production, productive, productivity and producer.
normal.cn: 同族词有 produce、product、production、productive、productivity 与 producer。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the commercial sense: product line, product launch, final product.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出商业义：产品线、产品发布、成品。

normal.en: The same word serves the reaction and the multiplication, which is why chemistry and arithmetic share it.
normal.cn: 同一个词既服务反应也服务乘法，所以化学与算术共用它。

normal.en: Product and by-product differ by one prefix: the second is what came out although nobody planned it.
normal.cn: product 与 by-product 只差一个前缀：后者是没人计划却照样出来的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a conveyor belt that ends exactly where the empty crates begin.
abstract.cn: 想象一条传送带的终点，正好是空料箱开始的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a child who repeats the habits of a school he later argues against.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子，重复着他后来反对的那所学校的习惯。

abstract.en: Picture two numbers meeting and leaving one number behind.
abstract.cn: 想象两个数相遇，留下一个数。

examples.en: The reaction produces a gas as its main product.
examples.cn: 这个反应的主要产物是一种气体。

examples.en: A product that nobody can repair will not keep its buyers.
examples.cn: 无人能修的产品留不住买家。

examples.en: The product of the two lengths gives the area of the rectangle.
examples.cn: 两条边的乘积给出矩形的面积。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pro（向前）+ duct（引导）」——把东西往前带出来的结果 → 产品、产物

root: 拉丁 ducere「引导」→ pro- 加 ducere 成 producere「引出」→ 过去分词 productum → 英语 product「被带出的东西」；16 世纪进入英语，商业义确切首见年代无定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act: something is led out of a process. The act then serves a reaction, a factory, a piece of work, a multiplication, a whole era, a farm, a studio and finally one shelf item.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：某物被从过程中引出来。这个动作随后服务于反应、工厂、一项工作、一次乘法、一个时代、一片农田、一家制片机构，最后是货架上的一个单品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the end of a conveyor belt where a finished object drops into a tray beside empty crates.
core.cn: 核心意象：传送带的尽头，一件成品落进托盘，旁边是空了的料箱。

branches.en: THE REACTION OUTPUT: a new substance appears where two others met.
branches.cn: 反应产出：两种物质相遇之处出现一种新物质。

branches.en: THE SHELF: a made item, and then one countable item inside a range.
branches.cn: 货架：一件制成品，再细化为系列中可数的一个单品。

branches.en: WORK AND MEDIA: knowledge, reports and films are brought out like goods.
branches.cn: 劳动与媒体：知识、报告与影片也像货物一样被带出来。

branches.en: ARITHMETIC: multiplication brings one number out of two.
branches.cn: 算术：乘法从两个数里带出一个数。

branches.en: WHAT GROWS OR SHAPES: crops grown from land, and people shaped by their time.
branches.cn: 长成或被塑造之物：田里长出的作物，与被时代塑造的人。

intro.en: Product is a Latin participle turned noun, and its prefix and verb stem still build a large English family.
intro.cn: product 是拉丁分词转成的名词，其前缀与动词词干仍在构建一个庞大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin producere and productum supply the stem, and ducere supplies a whole series of English verbs through its participle ductum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 producere 与 productum 提供词干，ducere 则通过其分词 ductum 提供了一整串英语动词。

items.example: The prefix adds the idea of bringing something out.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀加上「把某物带出来」的意思。

items.structure: ducere, duxi, ductum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The verb supplies the idea of leading.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「引导」的意思。

items.example: The Latin verb is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词是整个词族的来源。

items.example: The participle became a noun in its own right.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词本身变成了名词。

items.example: Water is the product of the reaction.

items.structure: pro- plus ducere, as a verb
items.example: The factory produces parts for bicycles.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂生产自行车零件。

items.example: Production rose after the line was rebuilt.
items.exampleCN: 生产线改建后产量上升。

items.example: The meeting was short and productive.
items.exampleCN: 这次会议简短而有成效。

items.example: Heat is a by-product of the reaction.
items.exampleCN: 热是这个反应的副产品。

items.example: The producer financed the whole shoot.
items.exampleCN: 制片人资助了整次拍摄。

definition_zh: 全部的；完整的；整个的；完整的事物；整体
definition_en: complete, with no part missing or broken, and the complete thing taken as one
core_image: 一只没被切开的圆苹果，皮从蒂到顶连成一圈，光亮完整
scene: 孩子捧着一只没切过的圆苹果，从皮到核全都还在，一口咬下去才第一次破开。 He ate the whole apple, including the core.
sceneCN: 这里 whole 是「全部的、完整的」（第 1 个义项：没有任何部分缺失或被切开）；句意为他吃掉了整个苹果，连核也没剩。那只从皮到蒂连成一圈、还没破开的圆苹果，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 完全地；全部地
完整性；健全
批发
全心全意的

senses.title: Complete, with nothing missing
senses.definition: having every part present, with nothing taken away or broken off
senses.definitionCN: 各部分都在，没有被取走或折断的地方
senses.example: He ate the whole apple, including the core.
senses.exampleCN: 他把整个苹果都吃了，连核也没剩。
senses.why: The oldest sense is sound and unbroken, so completeness is the base of everything else.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是健全、未破损，因此「完整」是其他一切意思的基础。

senses.title: The entire amount or period
senses.definition: used before a singular noun to mean all of it, the entire amount or time
senses.definitionCN: 用在单数名词前，表示该事物的全部或整段时间
senses.example: She spent the whole morning cleaning the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 她一整个上午都在打扫厨房。
senses.why: English prefers one whole noun to all the noun, so the adjective slides into counting.
senses.whyCN: 英语更爱说一个完整的名词，而不是「所有的」名词，于是这个形容词滑向了计数。

senses.title: The thing as one unit
senses.definition: the complete object or set seen as a single thing rather than as parts
senses.definitionCN: 把完整的东西或一整套看成单一之物，而不是各部分之和
senses.example: The parts were shipped separately and the whole was put together on site.
senses.exampleCN: 零件分别运来，整个东西在工地上组装起来。
senses.why: The noun keeps the picture of an unbroken object and simply removes the word for its parts.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时保留了那个未破开的物体形象，只是把「部分」的说法从视野里去掉。

senses.title: In good condition
senses.definition: in old or formal use, healthy and not damaged in body or mind
senses.definitionCN: 在旧式或正式用法中，指身心没有受损、健康无病
senses.example: The doctor said his mind was still whole after the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 医生说他摔倒后神志仍然健全。
senses.why: The Germanic root meant sound and healthy, and the physical sense of unbroken grew out of it.
senses.whyCN: 日耳曼语词根本来指健康无碍，未破损的物理意义正是从这里长出来的。

senses.title: In the fixed phrases
senses.definition: in on the whole meaning generally, and as a whole meaning together
senses.definitionCN: 用于 on the whole（总的来说）与 as a whole（作为一个整体）
senses.example: On the whole the plan worked well.
senses.exampleCN: 总的来说，这个计划运行得不错。
senses.why: The noun inside these phrases stands for everything counted together, an old habit of adding up.
senses.whyCN: 这些说法里的名词代表把一切加总起来，这是一种古老的计数习惯。

intro.en: Whole goes back to Old English hal, meaning sound, healthy and unhurt, the same root as heal and healthy.
intro.cn: whole 可上溯到古英语 hal，意为健全、健康、未受伤，与 heal、healthy 同根。

items.en: The root meant sound and without damage, describing a healthy body more than a full set.
items.cn: 这个词根表示健全、无损伤，更多描述健康的身体而非完备的集合。

items.en: Hal meant whole and healthy, and gave the verb haelian, to heal.
items.cn: hal 表示完整、健康，并派生动词 haelian（治愈）。

items.en: The w was added in spelling by analogy with who, and hol came to mean entire rather than sound.
items.cn: 中古英语时期受 who 影响在拼写中加入 w，hol 的词义也从「健全」转向「整个」。

items.en: The sense of complete and entire became the main one, while healthy kept the old health sense.
items.cn: 「完整、全部」成为主要意思，而健康义则由 healthy 继承下来。

items.en: Fixed phrases such as on the whole and as a whole gave the word a summing-up role.
items.cn: on the whole 与 as a whole 这类固定说法赋予它做总结的角色。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alike words that differ by one letter or sound, the second the words for complete and for a total.
note.cn: 第一组收只差一个字母或读音的形近词，第二组收表示完整与总体。

entries.definition: A gap or opening, pronounced exactly the same.
entries.definitionCN: 洞；孔

entries.definition: To make healthy again, from the same old root.
entries.definitionCN: 治愈

entries.definition: Completely, the adverb of whole.
entries.definitionCN: 完全地

entries.definition: The spelling that put a w into whole.
entries.definitionCN: 谁

entries.definition: Complete, often of an amount or a span.
entries.definitionCN: 整个的；全部的

entries.definition: The full amount counted together.
entries.definitionCN: 总的；全部的

entries.definition: The result of adding the parts up.
entries.definitionCN: 总数

normalIntro.en: Whole is the picture of an apple with no bite taken, and the silent w is the only trick in it.
normalIntro.cn: whole 就是一只没被咬过的苹果，唯一的陷阱是那个不发音的 w。

normal.en: Whole and hole sound identical; the w is decoration, the meaning is completeness.
normal.cn: whole 与 hole 读音相同；w 只是装饰，意思仍是完整。

normal.en: Heal and whole come from one family: to heal is to make sound again.
normal.cn: heal 与 whole 同族：治愈就是让它重新健全。

normal.en: On the whole is the same word used to add everything up.
normal.cn: on the whole 就是用这个词把一切加起来。

normal.en: Whole milk has not had the cream removed.
normal.cn: 全脂牛奶就是没有把奶油取走的牛奶。

normal.en: W-h-o-l-e keeps who at the start, why is a question you should skip.
normal.cn: whole 以 who 开头，不必追究那个 w 的来由。

abstract.en: Feel the smooth unbroken skin of an apple in the palm.
abstract.cn: 感觉掌心里苹果那层光滑未破的皮。

abstract.en: Hear a sound with no crack in it.
abstract.cn: 听一个没有裂纹的声音。

abstract.en: See a circle closed at the point where it started.
abstract.cn: 看见一个圆在起点处合拢。

examples.en: The whole village came out to watch the fireworks.
examples.cn: 全村的人都出来看烟花。

examples.en: On the whole, I think we made the right choice.
examples.cn: 总的来说，我认为我们的选择是对的。

examples.en: Two halves make a whole.
examples.cn: 两个半块合成一个整体。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「后」——后面什么都还在，一个不少，所以是完整的。

root: 日耳曼语词根（健全、无伤）→ 古英语 hal（完整、健康）→ 中古英语 whole（受 who 影响加 w）→ 现代英语 whole；同族有 heal、healthy、wholly。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with a body that is sound and unhurt, ships the physical sense of unbroken, then takes up all of a period, all of a thing, and the art of summing up.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从健全无伤的身体开始，随后带出未破损的物理意义，再接上整段时间、整个事物以及做总结的功能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an apple with no bite taken, the skin unbroken.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只没被咬过的苹果，皮是连着的。

branches.en: The apple branch: eaten whole, core and all.
branches.cn: 苹果分支：整个吃掉，连核也在内。

branches.en: The whole-morning branch: one long stretch of time.
branches.cn: 整个上午的分支：一整段时间。

branches.en: The assembly branch: parts shipped, the whole built on site.
branches.cn: 组装分支：零件运来，整体在现场装成。

branches.en: The health branch: a mind still whole after a fall.
branches.cn: 健康分支：摔倒后神志仍然健全。

branches.en: The summing branch: on the whole the plan worked.
branches.cn: 总结分支：总的来说计划可行。

intro.en: Whole is a free root with a silent w, and it builds adverbs and compounds with -ly, -ness and a first element such as whole- in wholesale.
intro.cn: whole 是带不发音 w 的自由词根，可用 -ly、-ness 派生副词与名词，也能作为前项构成 wholesale 一类复合词。

latinIntro.en: The native word has no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries below give the borrowed words that often translate it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个本土词没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁条目给出常用来翻译它的借入词。

items.example: It works as adjective and noun.
The noun is fixed in the frame.
items.exampleCN: 名词在这个框架中是固定的。
它在评价之前先做总结。

latinEntries.example: It gives the English word integer and entire.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它给出英语的 integer 与 entire。

definition_zh: 复制；抄写；模仿；复印；本；册；副本
definition_en: to make something the same as an original; a single book or a reproduction
core_image: 复印机的光一遍遍扫过，吐出和原件一模一样的纸
scene: 美术课上同桌的星星画得特别好看，我不由得照着画了一张。 I quietly copied her drawing of stars.
sceneCN: 这里 copy 是动词「模仿；照着画」（第 3 个义项：仿照原样制作）；句意是我悄悄照着她的星星画描了一张。

derivatives.zh: copy 与 book 合成，义为「习字帖」
由 copy 加 -ist 构成，义为「抄写员」
photo 与 copy 合成，义为「复印件」

senses.title: To make an exact reproduction
senses.definition: to make something exactly like the original
senses.definitionCN: 制作与原件一模一样的东西
senses.example: Please copy this page for everyone in the group.
senses.exampleCN: 请把这页复印给组里每个人。
senses.why: The core image is the machine that sends out twin pages.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是复印机吐出双胞胎纸页。

senses.title: To write out words from another source
senses.definition: to write the same words that you can see somewhere
senses.definitionCN: 照着某处可见的文字书写
senses.example: We copied the new words into our notebooks.
senses.exampleCN: 我们把生词抄进笔记本。
senses.why: Your hand follows the original line by line, a slower kind of copying.
senses.whyCN: 手一行行追随原件，是慢速的复制。

senses.title: To imitate someone or something
senses.definition: to do things the way another person does them
senses.definitionCN: 学着别人的样子做事
senses.example: Little brothers often copy what older ones do.
senses.exampleCN: 弟弟常模仿哥哥做的事。
senses.why: Imitation copies not paper but behaviour, the same idea applied to people.
senses.whyCN: 模仿复制的不是纸而是行为，是把同一概念用于人。

senses.title: A single book, newspaper or document
senses.definition: one single book, newspaper or document of many
senses.definitionCN: 许多相同书报中的一册
senses.example: There are only two copies of this magazine in the library.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆这本杂志只剩两本。
senses.why: Every printed book is a copy of one original text.
senses.whyCN: 每本印刷书都是某一原文本的复制品。

senses.title: A reproduction or duplicate
senses.definition: something made to be the same as an original
senses.definitionCN: 为与原件相同而做的东西
senses.example: Keep a copy of your ID card in your schoolbag.
senses.exampleCN: 书包里放一张身份证复印件。
senses.why: The noun names the twin itself, not the act.
senses.whyCN: 名词指那份孪生品，而非动作。

intro.en: Copy comes from Latin words about abundance, surprising as that sounds.
intro.cn: copy 出人意料地来自表示「充足」的拉丁词。

items.en: The Latin noun copia meant abundance or supply.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 copia 意为丰富、大量。

items.en: Writers used copia for the plenty of written material, giving the term copia libelli for a fair copy of a text.
items.cn: 作家用 copia 指大量文本，遂有 copia libelli 表示文本的誊清本。

items.en: Old French turned this into copie, a reproduction of a manuscript.
items.cn: 古法语变为 copie，指手稿的复本。

items.en: English adopted copy in the fourteenth century for written duplicates.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收 copy，指书面复本。

items.en: With printing and machines, copy spread to books, files and even imitating people.
items.cn: 随着印刷与机器，copy 扩展到书刊、文件，甚至指模仿人。

note.en: Some words share the copia root, others copy copy's shape.

normalIntro.en: Copy is twin-making in paper, ink and life.
normalIntro.cn: copy 是纸、墨和生活中的「孪生术」。

normal.en: copy comes from Latin copia, abundance of text.
normal.cn: copy 源自拉丁语 copia，文本之丰。

normal.en: copious shares the root and means plentiful.
normal.cn: copious 同根，意为大量的。

normal.en: copy the notes means write the same words.
normal.cn: copy the notes 指照抄同样的字。

normal.en: a copy of the book means one printed volume.
normal.cn: a copy of the book 指一册印刷书。

normal.en: copy sounds like copybei; typing copybei on a computer copies a file.

abstract.cn: 想象复印机的光扫过玻璃板。

abstract.en: Picture two identical snowflakes side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象两片一模一样的雪花并排。

abstract.en: Picture a little brother walking behind his big brother.
abstract.cn: 想象弟弟跟在哥哥身后学走路。

examples.en: Please do not copy answers during the exam.
examples.cn: 考试时请不要抄答案。

examples.en: This dictionary has more than one million copies in print.
examples.cn: 这本词典印量超过一百万册。

examples.en: Artists sometimes copy the old masters to learn brushwork.

sensesIntro.en: From abundant text to twins in paper and behaviour.

definition_zh: 丑陋的；难看的；丑恶的；险恶的；令人不快的
definition_en: unpleasant to look at, morally bad, or threatening in an unspecified way
core_image: 一张脸皱起来，让人本能地想转开眼睛
scene: 镜子前，孩子画的自画像把鼻子画得歪歪扭扭，他自己也忍不住捂住了嘴。 The drawing was so ugly that the whole class burst out laughing.
sceneCN: 这里 ugly 是「难看的、丑陋的」（第 1 个义项：外表不悦目）；句意为那幅画难看得全班都笑出了声。皱起的一张脸让人想转开眼睛，正是这个词的核心画面。

collocations.zh: 丑小鸭；起初不起眼而后出众的人

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「丑陋；丑恶」
形容词加 -ify 构成动词，义为「使变丑」
复合形容词，义为「样子难看的」

senses.title: Unpleasant to look at
senses.definition: unpleasant or unattractive in appearance
senses.definitionCN: 外表上令人不快、不好看的
senses.example: An ugly stain spread across the white tablecloth.
senses.exampleCN: 一块难看的污渍在白桌布上漫开。
senses.why: The word comes from Old Norse uggligr, which carried a sense of something to be dreaded, and the visual sense grew out of that dread.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自古诺斯语 uggligr，本带「令人畏惧」之意，视觉上的「难看」是从畏惧感里长出来的。

senses.title: Morally bad or shameful
senses.definition: morally offensive or shameful in a way that arouses disgust
senses.definitionCN: 道德上令人反感、使人厌恶的
senses.example: The trial exposed the ugly side of the business.
senses.exampleCN: 这场审讯暴露了这门生意丑恶的一面。
senses.why: From something dreadful to look at, the word easily moves to something dreadful to think about.
senses.whyCN: 从「看着可怕」很自然地滑到「想着可怕」，丑陋的外表就转成了丑陋的行为。

senses.title: Threatening or dangerous in an unclear way
senses.definition: used of a situation that looks threatening and may turn violent
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容看起来凶险、可能失控的局面
senses.example: The argument was starting to turn ugly.
senses.exampleCN: 争吵开始变得凶险起来。
senses.why: A scene that makes people wince is also a scene that may explode, so ugly marks rising tension.
senses.whyCN: 让人皱眉的场面往往也是随时会爆开的场面，于是 ugly 又用来标记气氛的紧张。

senses.title: Unpleasantly large or strong
senses.definition: used informally of an amount or problem that is unpleasantly big
senses.definitionCN: 非正式地形容数量或问题大得让人不舒服
senses.example: There is an ugly gap between the two reports.
senses.exampleCN: 两份报告之间有一道大得难看的鸿沟。
senses.why: Anything that makes you pull back your head can be called ugly, including an alarming figure.
senses.whyCN: 任何让你下意识缩头的东西都能叫 ugly，包括一个吓人的数字。

senses.title: Unattractive in a homely way
senses.definition: plain or ugly in appearance but not evil, often said of buildings or objects
senses.definitionCN: 外形朴素难看，但不含恶意，常用来形容建筑或器物
senses.example: They built an ugly block of flats by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在河边盖了一栋难看的公寓楼。
senses.why: This is the neutral everyday use: nothing dreadful, only an eye that refuses to rest on the thing.
senses.whyCN: 这是最中性的日常用法：并不可怕，只是眼睛不愿在它上面停留。

intro.en: The adjective is Scandinavian in origin and entered English in the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: 这个形容词源于斯堪的纳维亚语，中世纪进入英语。

items.en: Uggligr meant dreadful or to be feared, built on a root meaning fear.
items.cn: uggligr 意为「可怕的、令人畏惧的」，其词根表示恐惧。

items.en: The suffix -ligr corresponds to English -ly, so the word first described a manner rather than a face.
items.cn: 后缀 -ligr 相当于英语 -ly，因此这个词最早形容的是一种样子，而非一张脸。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the northern forms as ugly, still with the sense of fearful.
items.cn: 英语以北方方言形式借入作 ugly，仍保留「可怕」之义。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the sense of frightening had faded and appearance took over.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，「令人恐惧」的意味淡去，外观义占了上风。

items.en: Later centuries extend it to behaviour, situations, and amounts.
items.cn: 此后的几个世纪里，它又扩展到行为、局势与数量。

note.en: The look-alike group collects other -ly words, and the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of appearance.
note.cn: 形近组收集其他以 -ly 收尾的形容词，近义组汇集表示外观的其他形容词。

entries.definition: the quality of being ugly
entries.definitionCN: 丑陋；丑恶

entries.definition: very much, to a great degree
entries.definitionCN: 极其；非常（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: with strong interest
entries.definitionCN: 热切地（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: extremely ugly or unpleasant
entries.definitionCN: 极其丑陋的

entries.definition: not beautiful or decorated
entries.definitionCN: 相貌平平的；朴素的

entries.definition: not pleasing in appearance
entries.definitionCN: 不好看的；没有吸引力的

entries.definition: very pleasing to look at
entries.definitionCN: 美丽的

normalIntro.en: The word began as a label for what makes people afraid, and the sense slid from dread to looks.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起初标记让人害怕之物，意义由畏惧滑向外观。

normal.en: Ugly and dread share a northern origin, so a fearful shape becomes a bad-looking one.
normal.cn: ugly 与「畏惧」同出北方语言，可怕的样子就变成了难看的样子。

normal.en: Turn ugly is the phrase where the old fear still shows: the mood becomes dangerous.
normal.cn: turn ugly 这个搭配里还能看见旧日的恐惧：气氛变得危险。

normal.en: Ugly duckling comes from Andersen and means someone plain who grows remarkable.
normal.cn: ugly duckling 出自安徒生，指起初平平而后出众的人。

normal.en: Ugliness is the noun, uglify the verb that means to make ugly.
normal.cn: ugliness 是名词，uglify 是使变丑的动词。

normal.en: Uglier and ugliest double the final consonant before -er and -est.
normal.cn: 比较级 uglier 与最高级 ugliest 都在 -er 与 -est 前把 g 双写。

abstract.en: Picture a face in a funhouse mirror, features pulled sideways.
abstract.cn: 想象哈哈镜里的一张脸，五官被拉向一边。

abstract.en: Hear the crowd turn from laughter to a hard silence.
abstract.cn: 听人群从笑声转为僵硬的沉默。

abstract.en: Then feel the same discomfort when a number on a report is too large.
abstract.cn: 再把同样的不适感挪到一个报表上过大的数字。

examples.en: That building is the ugliest one on the street.
examples.cn: 那栋楼是街上最难看的一栋。

examples.en: The mood in the room turned ugly after the vote.
examples.cn: 投票之后屋里的气氛变得凶险。

examples.en: She refused to believe that an ugly past decides a bright future.
examples.cn: 她不肯相信一段丑恶的过去会决定一个光明的未来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿格丽」——阿格丽小姐一皱眉，整张脸就垮得让人不敢看。

root: 古诺斯语 uggligr（可怕的、可畏的），词根表示「恐惧」，后缀 -ligr 相当于英语 -ly；中古英语北方方言借入作 ugly

sensesIntro.en: One core feeling, unease at what meets the eye, spreads from faces to deeds, moods, and figures.
sensesIntro.cn: 一份核心感受，眼睛见到时的不适，由面孔蔓延到行为、气氛与数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face that makes you want to look away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张让人想转开眼睛的脸。

branches.en: The visual branch: faces, buildings, and objects that the eye rejects.
branches.cn: 视觉分支：眼睛拒绝停留的脸、建筑与器物。

branches.en: The moral branch, where a deed is as hard to look at as a scar.
branches.cn: 道德分支：一桩行为像伤疤一样让人不敢看。

branches.en: The mood branch, where a scene threatens to break open.
branches.cn: 气氛分支：场面随时可能炸开。

branches.en: The quantity branch, where a figure is unpleasantly large.
branches.cn: 数量分支：一个数字大得让人不适。

branches.en: The plain descriptive sense that most learners meet first.
branches.cn: 最朴素的描写义，也是学习者最先遇到的义项。

intro.en: The word is not built from Latin parts but from a northern suffix attached to a stem of fear.
intro.cn: 这个词不由拉丁部件构成，而是恐惧词干加北方语言后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor here, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 此词没有拉丁语祖先，故拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.example: Ugly once named what people feared.
items.exampleCN: ugly 曾经指人们畏惧的东西。

items.example: Ugly and lonely both end in -ly as adjectives.
items.exampleCN: ugly 与 lonely 都以 -ly 收尾而作形容词。

items.example: They uglified the square with billboards.
items.exampleCN: 他们用广告牌把广场弄得很难看。

items.example: The ugliness of the plan shocked them.
items.exampleCN: 计划的丑恶让他们震惊。

definition_zh: 第十一；十一分之一
definition_en: coming after ten others in order, or one part of eleven equal parts
core_image: 时钟两针重合指向十一点的那一格
scene: 比赛还剩最后一分钟，替补队员在场边热身。 The rescue came at the eleventh hour.
sceneCN: 这里 eleventh 是「第十一」（第 1 个义项：序数）；句意是救援在最后关头赶到。图中可辨识物件：计时刻度、场边热身者、奔来的救援队、终场哨。

senses.title: Position 11 in a series
senses.definition: coming after ten others in order
senses.definitionCN: 排在十个之后的位置。
senses.example: The rescue came at the eleventh hour.
senses.exampleCN: 救援在最后关头赶到。
senses.why: The ordinal suffix -th attaches to eleven, marking one step past the tenth.
senses.whyCN: 序数后缀 -th 附加于 eleven，标记第十之后的又一步。

senses.title: One of eleven equal parts
senses.definition: one part when a whole is divided into eleven equal parts
senses.definitionCN: 整体分成十一等份中的一份。
senses.example: Each heir took an eleventh of the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 每位继承人分得遗产的十一分之一。
senses.why: Ordinals double as fraction names, so eleventh also names a share.
senses.whyCN: 序数兼任分数名，eleventh 也指份额。

senses.title: The last possible moment
senses.definition: the very latest time something can happen, in the phrase the eleventh hour
senses.definitionCN: 习语 the eleventh hour 中指最迟的时间点。
senses.example: They signed the deal at the eleventh hour.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在最后一刻才签下协议。
senses.why: Old parables used the eleventh hour as the last chance, and the idiom survived.
senses.whyCN: 古老寓言把第十一个时辰当作最后机会，习语延续至今。

intro.en: Eleventh is eleven plus the old ordinal ending, with a famous idiom attached.
intro.cn: eleventh 是 eleven 加古老序数词尾，还挂着一条著名习语。

items.en: Old English endlefta formed the ordinal of endleofan.
items.cn: 古英语 endlefta 构成 endleofan 的序数形式。

items.en: Proto-Germanic ordinal patterns put the marker at the end.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语序数模式把标记放在词尾。

items.en: Middle English eleventhe smoothed into eleventh.
items.cn: 中古英语 eleventhe 简化为 eleventh。

items.en: Modern English keeps eleventh, notable for the n before th.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 eleventh，n 与 th 相接颇为独特。

items.en: The idiom the eleventh hour spread from an old vineyard parable.
items.cn: the eleventh hour 习语由一则古老葡萄园寓言传播开来。

note.en: Two compact groups: ordinal neighbors and the phrase family.
note.cn: 两组紧凑集合：相邻序数与习语家族。

definition_zh: 悲伤的；难过的；令人难过的；可悲的
definition_en: feeling unhappy; showing sorrow; making people feel unhappy; unfortunate and regrettable
core_image: 低着头、眼角含泪的一张脸
scene: 听到那个消息后，她显得很悲伤。 She looked sad after hearing the news.
sceneCN: 这里 sad 是「悲伤的、难过的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：听到那个消息后，她显得很悲伤。

pos.zh: 令人难过的；令人悲伤的

derivatives.zh: 悲伤地；遗憾地
悲伤；难过
使悲伤；使难过

senses.title: Feeling unhappy
senses.definition: feeling unhappy because something painful has happened
senses.definitionCN: 因发生痛苦的事而感到不快乐的
senses.example: She looked sad when she heard the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到这个消息时，她显得很悲伤。
senses.why: The core sense is low spirits inside a person.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是人内心低落的情绪。

senses.title: Causing sorrow
senses.titleCN: 令人难过的；令人悲伤的
senses.definition: making people feel unhappy or full of sorrow
senses.definitionCN: 使人感到不快或充满悲伤的
senses.example: It was a sad story about a lost child.
senses.exampleCN: 那是一个关于走失孩子的悲伤故事。
senses.why: The feeling spreads from people to what causes it.
senses.whyCN: 情绪从人扩展到引起情绪的事物。

senses.title: Regrettable
senses.definition: unfortunate and disappointing in a way that brings sorrow
senses.definitionCN: 不幸且令人失望、使人感到悲伤的
senses.example: It is sad that so many people were left out.
senses.exampleCN: 这么多人被排除在外，实在令人遗憾。
senses.why: Sorrow becomes a judgment on a situation.
senses.whyCN: 悲伤转为对某种处境的评判。

intro.en: Sad comes from Old English sæd, which first meant sated or weary.
intro.cn: sad 源自古英语 sæd，最初意为「吃饱的、疲倦的」。

items.en: Sæd means sated or weary.
items.cn: 古英语 sæd 意为吃饱的或疲倦的。

items.en: Fullness turns into weariness of spirit.
items.cn: 「饱足」引申为精神上的厌倦。

items.en: Sad comes to mean sorrowful.
items.cn: 中古英语中 sad 转为「悲伤的」。

items.en: Sad settles as the common word for sorrow.
items.cn: 近代早期英语中 sad 固定为表示悲伤的常用词。

items.en: Sad describes people, news, and situations.
items.cn: 现代英语中 sad 可形容人、消息与处境。

note.en: Sad means sorrowful; said is the past of say.

normalIntro.en: Sad appears whenever something painful or disappointing happens.
normalIntro.cn: 当痛苦或失望的事情发生时，就会用到 sad。

normal.en: She felt sad when her friend moved away.
normal.cn: 朋友搬走时，她感到很难过。

normal.en: The film has a sad ending.
normal.cn: 这部电影有一个悲伤的结局。

normal.en: He gave a sad smile and said nothing.
normal.cn: 他悲伤地笑了笑，什么也没说。

normal.en: It is sad to see the old shop close.
normal.cn: 看到老店关门，令人难过。

normal.en: The letter brought sad news from home.
normal.cn: 这封信带来了家里的悲伤消息。

abstract.en: Picture a face with lowered eyes and a heavy heart.
abstract.cn: 想象一张低垂双眼、心情沉重的脸。

abstract.en: Imagine rain falling on an empty playground.
abstract.cn: 想象雨落在空无一人的操场上。

abstract.en: Think of a song that slows down at the end.
abstract.cn: 想象一首在结尾放慢的歌曲。

examples.en: She was sad to leave her childhood home.
examples.cn: 离开童年的家让她很难过。

examples.en: The sad news spread through the village.
examples.cn: 这个令人难过的消息传遍了村庄。

examples.en: It is sad that the concert was cancelled.
examples.cn: 音乐会被取消，实在令人遗憾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sad」谐音「散的」：曲终人散，心里难免悲伤。

root: 源自古英语 sæd（吃饱的、厌倦的），由「饱足而生倦」引申为「心情低落、悲伤」。

sensesIntro.en: Sad means feeling unhappy, causing sorrow, or being unfortunate and regrettable.
sensesIntro.cn: sad 意为感到不快、令人悲伤的，或不幸而令人遗憾的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face lowered by sorrow.
core.cn: 核心意象：因悲伤而低垂的一张脸。

branches.en: The base sense is inner unhappiness.
branches.cn: 基础义是内心的不快。

branches.en: Feeling spreads to what causes it.
branches.cn: 情绪扩展到引起它的对象。

branches.en: Sorrow becomes a judgment on events.
branches.cn: 悲伤转为对事件的评判。

branches.en: A person and a story can both be sad.
branches.cn: 人与故事都可以是悲伤的。

branches.en: Sad news and a sad outcome overlap.
branches.cn: 悲伤的消息与可悲的结果相互重叠。

intro.en: Sad is a Germanic word that builds a small family with -ly, -ness, and -en.
intro.cn: sad 是日耳曼语词，通过 -ly、-ness 与 -en 构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Sad has no Latin root; it comes from Old English sæd.
latinIntro.cn: sad 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语 sæd。
