items.exampleCN: 这个消息让大家很悲伤。
一只眼神悲伤的狗在外面等候。
那位面带悲伤的男子什么也没说。

definition_zh: 化学；化学性质；（人与人的）微妙关系
definition_en: the science of substances and how they change; the chemical nature of something; a strong natural understanding between people
core_image: 实验台上排开的试管与天平，把物质拆开又合上
scene: 新学期的第一节化学课，老师在黑板上写下了水的分子式。 We have chemistry classes twice a week this term.
sceneCN: 这里 chemistry 是「化学」（第 1 个义项：研究物质的科学）；句意为这学期我们每周有两节化学课。

pos.zh: 化学；化学性质；人际默契

forms.label: 复数（指多种化学性质时）

derivatives.zh: 由 chemistry 变形加 -al 构成，义为「化学的；化学制品」
由 chemistry 变形加 -ist 构成，义为「化学家；药剂师」

senses.title: The science of substances and their changes
senses.definition: the science that studies what things are made of and how they change
senses.definitionCN: 研究物质构成及其变化的科学
senses.example: We have chemistry classes twice a week this term.
senses.exampleCN: 这学期我们每周有两节化学课。
senses.why: From the old craft of alchemy grew a proper science, keeping a form of the old name.
senses.whyCN: 从古老的炼金术成长出一门真正的科学，名字仍带着旧术的影子。

senses.title: The chemical nature of something
senses.definition: the chemical parts and behaviour of a particular thing
senses.definitionCN: 某物所含的化学成分及其表现
senses.example: The chemistry of sea water keeps many salts.
senses.exampleCN: 海水的化学性质使其含有很多盐分。
senses.why: A science name can also stand for the subject matter of one thing, its own make-up.
senses.whyCN: 学科之名也可指某一事物自身的成分构成。

senses.title: A natural understanding between people
senses.titleCN: （人与人之间的）默契；来电的感觉
senses.definition: a strong natural feeling that makes people get along well
senses.definitionCN: 使人与人自然投合的强烈感觉
senses.example: The two singers have great chemistry on stage.
senses.exampleCN: 两位歌手在台上配合得天衣无缝。
senses.why: People mix like substances: when the combination works, we borrow the science word for it.
senses.whyCN: 人与人像物质一样相互「反应」：组合得当时，我们便借这门学科之名。

intro.en: Chemistry grew out of alchemy, the old craft that tried to turn metals into gold.
intro.cn: chemistry 由炼金术发展而来，那门试图点石成金的古老技艺。

items.en: The ultimate root is uncertain: Egyptian keme (black earth), Greek chuma (poured metal) and Arabic al-kimiya are all candidates.
items.cn: 终极词根存疑：埃及语 keme（黑土）、希腊语 chuma（浇注的金属）与阿拉伯语 al-kimiya 均为候选。

items.en: Arabic al-kimiya carried the craft through the Islamic world.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-kimiya 使这门技艺传遍伊斯兰世界。

items.en: Medieval Latin alchemia named the gold-seeking craft in Europe.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 alchemia 在欧洲指寻金之术。

items.en: French chimie dropped the magical idea and named the new science.
items.cn: 法语 chimie 摒弃秘术色彩，命名新兴科学。

items.en: English chemistry settled in the seventeenth century for the science of substances.
items.cn: 英语 chemistry 于十七世纪定型，指研究物质的科学。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects sciences and teamwork words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收学科与默契类词。

entries.definition: Of chemistry; a chemical substance.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词/名词，义为「化学的；化学制品」，由 chemistry 派生。

entries.definition: A chemistry scientist or pharmacist.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「化学家；药剂师」，由 chemistry 派生。

entries.definition: A pipe carrying smoke away.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「烟囱」，读音与 chemistry 词首相近。

entries.definition: The science of energy and motion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「物理」，与 chemistry 并列的科学。

entries.definition: The science of living things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「生物」，与 chemistry 并列的科学。

entries.definition: A friendly understanding between people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「融洽关系」，与 chemistry 的默契义相近。

normalIntro.en: Remember chemistry by its root and family.
normalIntro.cn: 借助词根与词族记忆 chemistry。

normal.en: chemistry grew from alchemy, the gold-making craft.
normal.cn: chemistry 由炼金术（alchemy）发展而来。

normal.en: chemist and chemical both come from chemistry.
normal.cn: chemist 与 chemical 都由 chemistry 派生。

normal.en: a chemistry lab is where experiments happen.
normal.cn: chemistry lab 是做实验的地方。

normal.en: organic chemistry studies carbon substances.
normal.cn: 有机化学研究含碳物质。

normal.en: good chemistry between people means they work well together.
normal.cn: 人与人 good chemistry 意为配合默契。

abstract.en: Picture a bubbling flask glowing over a small flame.
abstract.cn: 想象小灯焰上微微发光的冒泡烧瓶。

abstract.en: Hear the squeak of chalk writing a formula.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见粉笔写公式的吱吱声。

abstract.en: Feel the click when two people just understand each other.
abstract.cn: 感受两人一拍即合时心灵的「咔哒」声。

examples.en: We have chemistry classes twice a week this term.
examples.cn: 这学期我们每周有两节化学课。

examples.en: The two singers have great chemistry on stage.
examples.cn: 两位歌手在台上配合默契。

root: 存疑源头（埃及语 keme 或希腊语 chuma）→ 阿拉伯语 al-kimiya → 中世纪拉丁语 alchemia → 法语 chimie → 英语 chemistry；同族词有 chemical（化学的）、chemist（化学家）、alchemist（炼金术士）。

sensesIntro.en: Chemistry spreads from the science to the make-up of things and human rapport.
sensesIntro.cn: chemistry 由科学学科延伸到事物的化学构成与人际默契。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the old art of changing matter, now a science
core.cn: 核心意象：从点金之术到物质科学

branches.cn: 配合完美的搭档

intro.en: Chemistry is alchemy with the old magic trimmed away and the science ending added.
intro.cn: chemistry 去掉了炼金术的神秘色彩，加上科学词尾。

latinIntro.cn: 中世纪词根 alchemia 是其直接祖先。

definition_zh: 旅行；出行；游历；传播；移动
definition_en: to go from one place to another, especially over a long distance
core_image: 背起行囊离开熟悉的地方，一路向前走到陌生的城市
scene: 暑假一开始，很多人收拾行李离开家乡。 They plan to travel across Europe by train this summer.
sceneCN: 这里 travel 是「旅行、出游」（第 1 个义项：从一个地方前往另一个地方）；句意是他们计划今年夏天乘火车横穿欧洲旅行。

derivatives.zh: travel 加表示人的后缀 -er，义为「旅行者；旅客」
travel 的现在分词作形容词，义为「旅行的；巡回的」

senses.title: To go from one place to another
senses.definition: to make a journey from one place to another, especially a long one
senses.definitionCN: 从一个地方前往另一个地方，尤指长途的行程
senses.example: They travelled to Japan for their holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们去日本度假旅行。
senses.why: The core image is leaving familiar ground and covering distance, so the first sense is simply making a journey.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是离开熟悉的地方、跨过距离，所以第一个义项就是「进行一次旅程」本身。

senses.title: To move or be carried from place to place
senses.definition: to move or be moved from one place to another as part of a journey or a route
senses.definitionCN: 沿路线移动或被运送，从一处到另一处
senses.example: The mail travels by plane and train.
senses.exampleCN: 邮件经飞机和火车运送。
senses.why: If people can travel, things and vehicles can follow routes too, so the image widens to any movement along a path.
senses.whyCN: 人能出行，物品和交通工具也能沿路线移动，画面就从「人旅行」扩展到「任何沿路径的运动」。

senses.title: To spread from one place to another
senses.definition: to spread or pass from one person, place, or thing to others, such as news, disease, or light
senses.definitionCN: 消息、疾病、光等从一处传到另一处；传播、蔓延
senses.example: The virus travelled quickly through the city.
senses.exampleCN: 病毒在城市里迅速传播。
senses.why: Movement from place to place applies to intangible things too, so the image of covering distance grows into spreading.
senses.whyCN: 「从一处到另一处」同样适用于无形之物，跨越距离的画面自然延伸为「传播、蔓延」。

senses.title: To move fast or with effort
senses.definition: to move with speed, or to move a machine part quickly along a track
senses.definitionCN: 以很快的速度移动；机器部件沿轨道快速滑动
senses.example: The bullet travelled through the air.
senses.exampleCN: 子弹在空中飞驰而过。
senses.why: Covering distance can be fast and forceful, so the same movement sense stretches to high speed and machine parts.
senses.whyCN: 跨越距离可以是快速而有力的，同一「移动」义便延伸到高速运动与机械部件的滑动。

senses.title: The activity of taking journeys
senses.definition: the activity of making journeys, especially as a general habit or industry
senses.definitionCN: 旅行这一活动本身，尤指作为习惯或行业
senses.example: Travel broadens the mind.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行开阔眼界。
senses.why: When the action of moving from place to place is named as a thing, it becomes the noun sense of travel.
senses.whyCN: 当「从一地到另一地」这个动作被当作一件事来称呼时，就形成了 travel 的名词义项。

senses.title: A journey or series of journeys
senses.definition: a journey, or the journeys that someone makes, often used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 一次旅程，或某人经历的多段旅程，常用复数
senses.example: She wrote a book about her travels in Asia.
senses.exampleCN: 她写了一本关于亚洲游历的书。
senses.why: The noun can also count the journeys themselves, so a whole trip or lifetime of trips is called travels.
senses.whyCN: 名词还可以把旅程本身作为对象来数说，于是整段行程或一生的游历被称为 travels。

senses.title: To move a machine part along a path
senses.definition: to move a part of a machine, or the distance that such a part can move
senses.definitionCN: 机器部件沿路径移动；也指部件可移动的距离即行程
senses.example: The piston travels up and down the cylinder.
senses.exampleCN: 活塞在气缸内上下移动。
senses.why: Machines copy the image of moving along a path, and the measured distance of that path becomes a technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 机械复制了「沿路径移动」的画面，这条路径的长度又被量化，形成技术上的「行程」义。

senses.title: To pass over a distance with speed
senses.definition: to pass over a particular distance, said of balls, light, sound, and similar things
senses.definitionCN: 球、光、声音等在空间中掠过某段距离
senses.example: The ball travelled twenty metres before it landed.
senses.exampleCN: 球飞出二十米才落地。
senses.why: Light, sound, and balls also cross distances, so the movement image covers any object passing over space.
senses.whyCN: 光、声音、球体同样会跨越距离，「跨越空间」的画面便涵盖一切掠过距离的物体。

intro.en: Travel goes back to the Latin word for a work tool, and its painful origin still hides inside the friendly modern word.
intro.cn: travel 的源头是拉丁语中表示「劳作工具」的词，它 painful 的本义仍藏在今天轻松的旅行一词背后。

items.en: Latin trepalium is generally thought to have meant an instrument of torture, though the exact form of the device is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁语 trepalium 指一种刑具，但该器械的具体形制已不可考。

items.en: Old French travailler came to mean to toil, to labor painfully, and travailler appeared by the twelfth century.
items.cn: 古法语 travailler 至十二世纪已表示「辛苦劳作、艰难做工」。

items.en: Middle English adopted travailen in the sense of to toil and to struggle, and it also meant to make a journey, because journeys were hardship.
items.cn: 中古英语借用 travailen，既表示「劳苦、挣扎」，也表示「长途跋涉」，因为那时的旅程本身就是苦役。

items.en: In the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries the word split into travail, which kept the meaning of painful labor, and travel, which kept the meaning of journeying.
items.cn: 十五至十六世纪，该词分化为 travail（保留「辛劳」义）和 travel（保留「旅行」义）。

items.en: Modern English travel keeps the journey sense for people, goods, light, and news, while travail survives as a formal word for painful effort.
items.cn: 现代英语中 travel 用于人、货物、光线、消息的移动，travail 则作为正式用词保留「艰辛劳作」之义。

note.en: Travel has a famous look-alike from the same ancestor, and several journey words sit close to it in meaning.
note.cn: travel 有一个同源的著名形近词，另有一些表示「旅程」的词在意义上与之相近。

entries.definition: painful or laborious effort; the older sister of travel
entries.definitionCN: 艰辛的劳作或痛苦的努力；与 travel 同源，是保留古义的「兄弟词」

entries.definition: a person who is travelling; British double-l spelling
entries.definitionCN: 旅行者；英式拼写为双写 l，美式写作 traveler

entries.definition: to cross or pass over an area; only spelling resembles travel, root is different
entries.definitionCN: 横越、穿过某区域；只是拼写与 travel 相近，词源不同（源自拉丁 trans-versus）

entries.definition: an act of traveling from one place to another, especially a long one
entries.definitionCN: 从一地到另一地的行程，尤指长途旅行；作名词为主

entries.definition: a long journey by sea or in space
entries.definitionCN: 经海路或太空的长途航行；travel 不限交通方式

entries.definition: a journey for pleasure during which you visit several places
entries.definitionCN: 以观光为目的、辗转多地的旅行；travel 泛指出行行为

normalIntro.en: Use the shared ancestor travail to link travel with its family and set phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 利用共同祖先 travail 把 travel 与词族和固定搭配串起来记。

normal.en: travel comes from the same French root as travail: long journeys once meant hard labor.
normal.cn: travel 与 travail 同源：旧时长途跋涉就是一场苦役。

normal.en: tra-vel sounds like tuo-lei, dragging a tired body to a faraway place is exactly what a traveler does.
normal.cn: 「拖-累」谐音：拖着疲惫的身体去外地，正是旅行。

normal.en: travel light: light does double duty, few luggage and easy movement.
normal.cn: 搭配 travel light 里 light 一语双关：行李少，脚步轻。

normal.en: traveler = travel + -er, the person who does the traveling.
normal.cn: traveler 就是 travel 加 -er，做出旅行动作的人。

normal.en: news travels fast: even news travels, so the movement sense covers almost everything.
normal.cn: _news travels fast_ 连消息都会「跑」，可见 travel 的移动义几乎无处不在。

abstract.en: Picture your suitcase rolling away from your door on its own, drawing a long line across the map.
abstract.cn: 想象行李箱自己滚出家门，在地图上拖出一条长长的线——那就是 travel 的路径。

abstract.en: Feel the train window: trees slide backward, distance shrinks, you are the one moving.
abstract.cn: 感受车窗外的树向后滑去、距离被缩短——移动的就是你，这就是 travel 的核心。

abstract.en: A rumor whispers in one ear and leaves from another, hopping from city to city like a tiny traveler.
abstract.cn: 谣言在耳边低语又飞走，像一个小小的旅行者 hop 一城又一城——传播也是 travel。

examples.en: They plan to travel across Europe by train.
examples.cn: 他们计划乘火车横穿欧洲旅行。

examples.en: Her travels in Asia lasted almost two years.
examples.cn: 她在亚洲的游历持续了将近两年。

examples.en: Light travels faster than sound.
examples.cn: 光的传播速度比声音快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拖-累-哦」——拖着累兮兮的身子出门，一路奔波，就是 travel（旅行）。

root: travel 与 travail 同出古法语 travailler（劳作、辛苦做工），后者来自一般认为的拉丁语 trepalium（一种刑具，形制存疑）。原义「苦役」引申为「艰难跋涉」，后分化为两个词：travail 保留辛劳义，travel 专指旅行。

sensesIntro.en: From the act of making a journey, travel spreads to goods and vehicles on routes, to news and disease that spread, and finally to the noun for journeys themselves.
sensesIntro.cn: travel 从「进行旅程」出发，扩展到货物与交通工具的运送，再到消息与疾病的传播，最后形成指旅程本身的名词义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: leaving familiar ground and covering the distance to somewhere else
core.cn: 核心意象：离开熟悉的地面，跨过通向远方的距离

branches.en: People travel when they make journeys to far places.
branches.cn: 人前往远方旅行，对应「出游」义。

branches.en: Goods, mail, pistons, and balls also travel along routes and distances.
branches.cn: 货物、邮件、活塞、球体沿路线与距离移动，对应「运送」与「行程」义。

branches.en: News, viruses, and light travel from one place to many.
branches.cn: 消息、病毒、光向各处扩散，对应「传播」义。

branches.en: Bullets and fast machines travel with great speed.
branches.cn: 子弹与高速机械飞驰，对应「快速行进」义。

branches.en: The whole activity and the counted journeys become the noun travel and travels.
branches.cn: 整个活动与多段旅程固化为名词 travel 与 travels。

intro.en: Travel itself is a plain root, but the family around it uses common noun, agent, and adjective endings.
intro.cn: travel 本身是一个朴素的词根，其词族借助常见的名词、施动者与形容词后缀扩展。

senses.title: The Square Says Yes: conforming to the rule
senses.definition: typical, common, or in accordance with an established standard
senses.definitionCN: 典型的、常见的，或符合既定标准的
senses.example: The machine was running at normal speed.
senses.exampleCN: 机器以正常速度运转。
senses.why: Late Latin normalis meant 'in conformity with rule' and classical Latin described something 'made according to a carpenter's square'. What the square accepts is normal; what it rejects is not.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁语 normalis 意为“合乎规矩”，古典拉丁语则指“按木工尺做成的”。尺子认可的就是 normal，尺子拒绝的就不是。

senses.title: The Right Angle: perpendicular in geometry
senses.definition: standing at a right angle to a line or surface, as a geometric relation
senses.definitionCN: 与一条线或一个面成直角，指几何关系
senses.example: The normal line meets the curve at exactly ninety degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 法线与曲线恰好成九十度相交。
senses.why: A carpenter's square exists to make right angles. The 1640s geometry sense simply states the tool's job in mathematical language: a normal line is square to the surface.
senses.whyCN: 木工尺存在的目的就是做出直角。17 世纪 40 年代的几何义只是用数学语言说出这件工具的职责：法线与面成直角。

senses.title: Business as Usual: the ordinary standard
senses.definition: conforming to common standards or the established order of things
senses.definitionCN: 符合通行标准或事物的既定秩序
senses.example: Normal service resumed after the power cut.
senses.exampleCN: 停电之后服务恢复正常。
senses.why: Once the square stands for the established order, anything that follows that order is normal. The 1828 sense generalizes the geometrical rule into everyday standards.
senses.whyCN: 当尺子代表既定秩序，任何顺着这个秩序的东西就是 normal。1828 年的义项把几何规矩推广为日常标准。

senses.title: Within the Healthy Range
senses.definition: healthy or functioning within the expected range, used of bodies and body readings
senses.definitionCN: 健康或在预期范围内运作，用于身体及各项读数
senses.example: Her blood pressure was normal for her age.
senses.exampleCN: 就她的年龄而言，血压正常。
senses.why: Medicine measures a body against a range taken from healthy people. A reading inside that range conforms to the rule, so it is called normal.
senses.whyCN: 医学用取自健康人群的范围来量身体。落在这个范围内的读数合乎规矩，于是被称作正常。

senses.title: The Bell Curve: statistically typical
senses.titleCN: 钟形曲线：统计上的典型
senses.definition: falling at or near the average of a statistical distribution
senses.definitionCN: 位于统计分布的均值处或附近
senses.example: Most measurements cluster around the normal value.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数测量值聚集在正常值附近。
senses.why: Statistics turns the rule into a curve: most cases pile up at the middle, and that middle is the normal value. Being near it is being typical.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把规矩变成一条曲线：多数个案堆在中间，中间就是正常值。靠近它就是典型。

senses.title: Nothing Special: ordinary and unremarkable
senses.titleCN: 没有什么特别：普通平常
senses.definition: ordinary and not special or surprising, used of events and days
senses.definitionCN: 普通、不特别也不令人意外的，用于事件和日子
senses.example: It was a normal Tuesday, with nothing unusual at all.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个平常的星期二，没有任何异常。
senses.why: The standard case is also the unexciting case. When nothing departs from the rule, the day is merely normal.
senses.whyCN: 标准情形也是不起眼的情形。当没有任何东西偏离规矩，这一天就只是 normal。

senses.title: Back to Normal: the usual state
senses.definition: the usual or expected state of affairs, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 通常或预期的事态，作名词使用
senses.example: After the storm, the town slowly returned to normal.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后，小镇慢慢恢复了常态。
senses.why: The adjective was turned into a noun in 1890: 'the normal' is the state that conforms to the rule. To return to normal is to line up with the square again.
senses.whyCN: 1890 年形容词转为名词：the normal 就是合乎规矩的状态。return to normal 就是重新与尺子对齐。

senses.title: The Perpendicular Line: a geometric noun
senses.definition: a line or plane perpendicular to a given line, surface, or curve
senses.definitionCN: 与给定直线、平面或曲线垂直的线或面
senses.example: Drop a normal from the point to the base line.
senses.exampleCN: 从该点向基线作一条法线。
senses.why: The noun use of 1727 names the very line the square draws. A normal is the line that stands at a right angle, the geometric object behind the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 1727 年的名词用法命名的正是尺子画出的那条线。normal 就是那条成直角的线，是形容词背后的几何对象。

senses.title: The Standard-Setting School
senses.titleCN: 立标准的学校：师范学校
senses.definition: in normal school, a 19th-century teacher-training institution whose name meant 'setting the standard'
senses.definitionCN: normal school 指 19 世纪的师范学校，其名称理据是“用来设定标准的”
senses.example: The state opened its first normal school in 1839.
senses.exampleCN: 该州于 1839 年开办了第一所师范学校。
senses.why: Normal school was translated in 1835 from French école normale (1794). The school was named as the place that sets the standard for teachers, not as a place for 'ordinary' students.
senses.whyCN: normal school 于 1835 年译自法语 école normale（1794）。这所学校被命名为“为教师立标准的地方”，而不是“普通学生的地方”。

intro.en: Normal shares norma with norm, but it appeared much earlier and first meant 'conforming to rule' before it meant 'usual'. The geometrical sense came in the 1640s; the everyday sense 'standard, ordinary' is recorded in 1828.
intro.cn: normal 与 norm 同出 norma，但它出现得早得多，且先有“合乎规矩”义，后有“正常、通常”义。几何义出现于 17 世纪 40 年代；日常的“标准、普通”义记录于 1828 年。

items.en: First recorded with the sense 'typical, common', already applied to ordinary cases rather than to geometry.
items.cn: 最早记录的义项是“典型的、常见的”，已经用于普通情形，而不是几何。

items.en: The geometrical sense 'standing at a right angle, perpendicular' appears, drawing directly on the carpenter's square.
items.cn: 出现几何义“成直角的、垂直的”，直接取象于木工尺。

items.en: From Late Latin normalis 'in conformity with rule, normal'; in classical Latin the same word meant 'made according to a carpenter's square', from norma 'rule, pattern'.
items.cn: 来自晚期拉丁语 normalis“合乎规矩的、正常的”；古典拉丁语中这个词意为“按木工尺做成的”，出自 norma“规矩、范式”。

items.en: The sense 'conforming to common standards or established order' is recorded, possibly current earlier.
items.cn: 记录到“符合通行标准或既定秩序”的义项，可能在实际使用中更早。

items.en: Normal school is translated from French école normale (1794); the name means an institution that sets the standard.
items.cn: normal school 译自法语 école normale（1794）；这个名字的意思是“设定标准的机构”。

items.en: The noun 'normal state' is recorded in 1890, while the geometrical noun normal 'perpendicular line' dates from 1727. Both keep the image of a line drawn square to something.
items.cn: 名词“常态”记录于 1890 年，而几何名词 normal“垂直线”始于 1727 年。两者都保留了“与某物成直角的一条线”的意象。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the same norma family; the near-meaning group holds words that overlap with only part of normal.
note.cn: 形近组是同一个 norma 词族；近义组是只与 normal 部分义项重叠的词。

entries.definition: the standard itself. Normal is the adjective saying that something conforms to it.
entries.definitionCN: 标准本身。normal 是形容词，表示某物合乎这个标准。

entries.definition: prescribing what should be done, not describing what is usual. Normal describes fact; normative sets a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 规定应该怎么做，而不是描述通常怎样。normal 描述事实，normative 立规矩。

entries.definition: departing from the normal. The ab- prefix means 'away from', the exact opposite of conforming.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离正常的。前缀 ab- 意为“离开”，正是“合乎”的反面。

entries.definition: not special or unusual. It stresses lack of distinction, while normal stresses conformity to a standard.
entries.definitionCN: 不特别、不稀奇。它强调“不出众”，normal 强调“合乎标准”。

entries.definition: showing the usual qualities of a group. It points to a representative example, not to a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 体现某类事物通常特征的。它指向代表性样本，而不是规矩。

entries.definition: an established level or rule. It is the noun behind normal; normal is what meets that level.
entries.definitionCN: 既定的水平或规则。它是 normal 背后的名词；normal 就是达到该水平的。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: normal and norm both come from norma, the carpenter's square, and the geometry sense still shows the tool at work.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想是真实的：normal 与 norm 都出自 norma（木工尺），而几何义至今仍能看出这件工具在工作。

normal.en: Normalis in Late Latin meant 'in conformity with rule'; the rule was norma, the carpenter's square.
normal.cn: 晚期拉丁语 normalis 意为“合乎规矩”，而规矩就是 norma，那把木工尺。

normal.en: Normal and norm share norma, but normal is older and started from 'conforming to rule', not from 'usual'.
normal.cn: normal 与 norm 共用 norma，但 normal 更早，而且起点是“合乎规矩”，不是“通常”。

normal.en: In geometry a normal line is square to a surface: the tool's right angle turned into a line.
normal.cn: 几何中的法线与面成直角：工具的直角变成了一条线。

normal.en: Return to normal is a fixed phrase: the state that lines up with the square again.
normal.cn: return to normal 是固定说法：重新与尺子对齐的状态。

normal.en: A normal school was a standard-setting school for teachers, not a school for ordinary people.
normal.cn: normal school 是为教师立标准的学校，不是给普通人办的学校。

abstract.en: Picture a level on a wall: the bubble sits in the middle and the wall is declared true.
abstract.cn: 想象一把水平尺贴在墙上：气泡停在中间，这堵墙就被判为端正。

abstract.en: The same middle position becomes health: a reading inside the expected range is normal.
abstract.cn: 同一个中间位置变成健康：落在预期范围内的读数就是正常。

abstract.en: Move the frame to a crowd and the middle becomes the average person; normal is the crowd's centre line.
abstract.cn: 把框架移到人群，中间就成了平均人；normal 就是人群的中心线。

examples.en: Under normal circumstances, the ferry crosses the river every hour.
examples.cn: 正常情况下，渡轮每小时过河一次。

examples.en: The doctor said the results were normal and no treatment was needed.
examples.cn: 医生说结果正常，不需要治疗。

examples.en: It took three days for the airport to return to normal after the snow.
examples.cn: 大雪过后机场用了三天才恢复正常。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺默」——大家都点头应“诺”、默认照做 → normal 正常的、标准的

root: 拉丁语 normalis“合乎规矩的”，出自 norma“木工尺、规矩”；与 norm 同源，先有“合乎规矩”，后有“正常、通常”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of normal all come from one act: laying a square against something. Wood, walls, bodies, numbers and schools are each checked against a rule, and whatever fits is called normal.
sensesIntro.cn: normal 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：把尺子贴在某物上。木头、墙壁、身体、数字和学校都要对着规矩检查，对得上的就叫 normal。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a level or square laid against a surface, with no tilt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把水平尺或直角尺贴在表面上，没有倾斜。

branches.en: CONFORMITY: fitting the rule, then fitting the ordinary order of things.
branches.cn: 合乎：先合乎规矩，再合乎事物的日常秩序。

branches.en: GEOMETRY: the perpendicular direction and the perpendicular line itself.
branches.cn: 几何：垂直方向，以及垂直线本身。

branches.en: MEASURED BODIES AND NUMBERS: the healthy range and the centre of a distribution.
branches.cn: 被量度的身体与数字：健康范围与分布中心。

branches.en: THE UNREMARKABLE AND THE USUAL STATE: an ordinary day, and 'the normal' as a noun.
branches.cn: 平常与常态：普通的一天，以及名词 the normal。

branches.en: THE STANDARD-SETTING SCHOOL: normal school, named for the standard it sets.
branches.cn: 立标准的学校：normal school，因它所设定的标准而得名。

intro.en: Normal is norma plus the adjective suffix -alis, which becomes -al in English. The family then adds -ly, -ity, -ize and the negative prefix ab-.
intro.cn: normal 是 norma 加形容词后缀 -alis（进入英语作 -al）。词族随后再加 -ly、-ity、-ize 以及否定前缀 ab-。

latinIntro.en: Latin normalis 'in conformity with rule' comes from norma 'carpenter's square'. Its opposite branch is enormis 'out of rule', and the bare noun norma also gives English norm.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 normalis“合乎规矩”出自 norma“木工尺”。它的反义分支是 enormis“出了规矩”，而光秃名词 norma 也给了英语 norm。

abstract.cn: 视觉被送到远处的房间里。

abstract.en: One word holds machine, medium, and trade.
abstract.cn: 一个词容纳机器、媒介与行业。

abstract.en: The screen became the family fire.
abstract.cn: 屏幕成了家庭的火塘。

branches.en: The medium is the first sense.

branches.cn: 信号与屏幕是一套系统。

branches.cn: 机器与演播室互相依存。

intro.cn: television 衍生出 televise 与 televised。

definition_zh: 夜晚；夜间；晚上；天黑；艰难时期
definition_en: the dark period between sunset and sunrise; the hours spent asleep; an evening given to an event; the coming of darkness; and a figurative time of trouble
core_image: 楼道灯灭下去，路灯把树影拉进屋角
scene: 楼道里的声控灯灭下去，窗外的路灯把树影拉进屋角。 The city grows quiet at night.
sceneCN: 这里 night 是「夜晚」（第 1 个义项：日落到日出之间的黑暗时段）；句意为到了夜里，城市安静下来。图中可辨识物件：楼道灯、窗外路灯、树影。

derivatives.zh: 由 night 加 -ly 构成，义为「每夜的；每晚」
由 night 与 fall（落下）复合而成，义为「天黑；入夜」
由 mid（中间）与 night 复合而成，义为「午夜」
由 night 与 life 复合而成，义为「夜生活」

senses.title: The dark hours between sunset and sunrise
senses.definition: the period of darkness that begins at sunset and ends at sunrise
senses.definitionCN: 从日落开始到日出结束的那一段黑暗时间
senses.example: The streets are empty at night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里街上空无一人。
senses.why: The Old English noun named the dark half of the day, and the word has kept that simple division of the clock ever since.
senses.whyCN: 古英语的这个名词指的就是一天中黑暗的那一半，这个词至今仍守着钟面上这条简单的分界。

senses.title: A night spent asleep
senses.definition: the stretch of rest that a person gets between going to bed and waking
senses.definitionCN: 从上床到醒来之间那一段休息的时间
senses.example: She had a good night and woke up rested.
senses.exampleCN: 她睡了个好觉，醒来精神很好。
senses.why: Because the dark hours are the hours of sleep, the same word names the rest itself, so a good night is counted in hours slept rather than in anything seen.
senses.whyCN: 因为黑暗的那些小时正是睡觉的时辰，同一个词就用来指这段休息本身，所以「好的一夜」是按睡了多少小时来算，而不是按看见了什么。

senses.title: An evening given to an event
senses.definition: an evening set aside for a performance, a match or a social occasion
senses.definitionCN: 为演出、比赛或社交活动专门留出的那个晚上
senses.example: The opening night drew a full house.
senses.exampleCN: 首演之夜座无虚席。
senses.why: An event held after dark borrows the name of the time it fills, so the word can mean an evening handed over to a show or a game.
senses.whyCN: 天黑之后举办的活动会借用它所占据的时段的名字，所以这个词能指交给演出或比赛的那个晚上。

senses.title: The moment darkness falls
senses.definition: the point at which daylight ends and darkness comes down
senses.definitionCN: 白昼结束、黑暗降临的那一刻
senses.example: The light faded and night came down over the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 光线退去，夜幕落到山谷上方。
senses.why: Since the same noun can name a period and its edge, it also marks the arrival of darkness, which is why a sentence can say that night came down.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既能指一段时期，也能指它的边缘，所以它也标记黑暗的到来，这才有「夜幕落下」这样的句子。

senses.title: A time of gloom or trouble
senses.definition: a stretch of sorrow, fear or hardship felt as long and heavy as the dark hours
senses.definitionCN: 像黑夜一样漫长沉重的悲伤、恐惧或艰难时光
senses.example: The family went through a long night of worry before the results came.
senses.exampleCN: 结果出来之前，这家人熬过了一段漫长的担忧。
senses.why: Darkness has long served as a figure for trouble, so a night can stand for any spell of fear or grief that feels as though the light will never return.
senses.whyCN: 黑暗自古就被用来比喻困境，所以 night 能指任何一段恐惧或悲伤的时光，仿佛光再也不会回来。

intro.en: Night is one of the oldest words English owns, an Old English noun still close to its Germanic shape and related to Latin nox.
intro.cn: night 是英语里最古老的词之一，这个古英语名词至今仍贴近它的日耳曼语形态，并与拉丁语 nox 同源。

items.en: A reconstructed root usually written nokwt- stands behind the word in many Indo-European languages, though scholars still argue about its exact shape.
items.cn: 许多印欧语系语言中这个词背后都有一个通常写作 nokwt- 的重构词根，不过学者对它的确切形态仍有争论。

items.en: The Germanic noun nahts gave Old English its word and also stands behind German Nacht.
items.cn: 日耳曼语名词 nahts 给了古英语这个词，也是德语 Nacht 的来处。

items.en: Niht named the dark part of the day and already formed compounds such as nihtlic, the ancestor of nightly.
items.cn: niht 指一天中黑暗的部分，并已构成 nihtlic 这样的复合词，那是 nightly 的前身。

items.en: Middle English kept the spellings niht and night, and the gh stopped being pronounced, leaving the long vowel heard today.
items.cn: 中古英语保留 niht 与 night 两种写法，后来 gh 不再发音，只留下今天听到的长元音。

items.en: Modern English uses night for the dark hours, for an evening event and for a time of sorrow, while the gh in the spelling is a silent relic.
items.cn: 现代英语用 night 指黑暗的时段、某个活动的晚上以及悲伤的时期，而拼写里的 gh 是一块沉默的遗迹。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the homophone and the compounds built with this noun; the near-meaning group collects other words for the dark part of the day.
note.cn: 形近组收同音词与用这个名词构成的复合词；近义组收其他表示一天中黑暗时段的词。

entries.definition: A mounted soldier of the Middle Ages; it sounds exactly like night but comes from a different Old English word.
entries.definitionCN: 中世纪的骑马武士；与 night 读音完全相同，却出自另一个古英语词。

entries.definition: Happening or done every night.
entries.definitionCN: 每夜发生或做的。

entries.definition: The middle of the night, twelve o'clock at night.
entries.definitionCN: 夜的正中，夜间十二点。

entries.definition: A small brown bird famous for singing at night.
entries.definitionCN: 因夜间鸣唱而闻名的小型褐色鸟；夜莺。

entries.definition: The part of the day between afternoon and bedtime.
entries.definitionCN: 下午与就寝之间的那段时间；傍晚。

entries.definition: The darker stage of twilight, just before night.
entries.definitionCN: 暮色中最暗的阶段，紧挨着夜晚之前。

entries.definition: The absence of light, the quality that defines the night.
entries.definitionCN: 没有光的状态，正是夜晚之所以为夜的性质。

entries.definition: The period of the night, used as a plain label for the dark hours.
entries.definitionCN: 夜间的时段，用作指黑暗时间的平实说法。

normalIntro.en: The word is an old Germanic noun of night that English kept almost unchanged, with a silent gh in the spelling and a large family of compounds around it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个古老的日耳曼语「夜」名词，英语几乎原样保留，拼写里有个不发音的 gh，周围还有一大族复合词。

normal.en: The gh in the spelling was once a throaty sound, and it went silent while the vowel lengthened.
normal.cn: 拼写里的 gh 曾经是一个喉咙里的音，后来它不响了，元音反而变长。

normal.en: Night and knight sound the same today, though one is a time and the other a rider.
normal.cn: night 与 knight 今天读音相同，但一个是时间，一个是骑马的人。

normal.en: The -ly of nightly means every night, the same ending that appears in daily and weekly.
normal.cn: nightly 里的 -ly 表示「每夜」，与 daily、weekly 用的是同一个词尾。

normal.en: Midnight is simply the middle of the night, built the same way as midday.
normal.cn: midnight 就是夜的正中，构词方式与 midday 一样。

normal.en: German Nacht and Latin nox descend from the same old root, which is why night turns up across so many languages.
normal.cn: 德语 Nacht 与拉丁语 nox 出自同一个古老词根，所以「夜」在许多语言里都有相似的影子。

abstract.en: A word for the dark half of the clock becomes a word for an evening out and for a spell of grief, because darkness measures time in more than one way.
abstract.cn: 一个指钟面暗半边的词，又成了外出的一晚和一段悲伤的时光，因为黑暗可以用不止一种方式计量时间。

abstract.en: Night and knight are twins in sound and strangers in meaning, a reminder that spelling keeps an old history the mouth has dropped.
abstract.cn: night 与 knight 声音上是双胞胎，意义上却是陌路人，提醒人拼写保存着口腔早已丢掉的旧历史。

abstract.en: Every night is both a period and a beginning, which is why the same noun can mean the dark hours and the moment they arrive.
abstract.cn: 每一个夜晚既是一段时期，也是一个开端，所以同一个名词既能指黑暗的时段，也能指它降临的那一刻。

examples.en: The streets are empty at night.
examples.cn: 夜里街上空无一人。

examples.en: The opening night drew a full house.
examples.cn: 首演之夜座无虚席。

examples.en: She had a good night and woke up rested.
examples.cn: 她睡了个好觉，醒来精神很好。

definition_zh: 错误的；不对的；不合适的；错事；冤枉
definition_en: not correct or not true, not suitable, or to treat someone unfairly
core_image: 路牌指向岔路，走上去却发现前面是死胡同
scene: 岔路口的路牌被风吹歪了，一行人照着箭头走，最后停在断墙前。 You have the wrong number, said a voice on the phone.
sceneCN: 这里 wrong 是「错误的；不对的」（第 1 个义项：不正确、不真实的）；句意为电话那头说「你打错号码了」。被风吹歪的路牌把行人引到断墙前，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wrong 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「错误地；不公正地」
由 wrong 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「不当的；非法的」
由 wrong 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「错误；不当」
由 wrong 与 doing 复合构成，义为「坏事；不法行为」

senses.title: Not correct
senses.definition: not correct, not true, or not matching the facts
senses.definitionCN: 不正确、不真实或与事实不符
senses.example: You have the wrong number, said a voice on the phone.
senses.exampleCN: 电话那头有人说，你打错号码了。
senses.why: The oldest sense is twisted or crooked, and a crooked line is the plainest picture of something not straight, that is, not correct.
senses.whyCN: 最早的意思是「扭的、歪的」，歪斜的线就是「不正」最直白的画面，即不正确。

senses.title: Not the right one
senses.definition: not suitable for a particular person, time, or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 对某个人、某个时间或某个用途不合适
senses.example: It was the wrong moment to ask for a raise.
senses.exampleCN: 那个时机提加薪是不合适的。
senses.why: If a thing is off the straight line, it is also off the fitting place, so unsuitability joins incorrectness.
senses.whyCN: 事物偏离直线，也就偏离了合适的位置，于是「不合适」与「不正确」并在一起。

senses.title: In the wrong way
senses.definition: in a way that is not correct, used as an adverb without -ly in everyday speech
senses.definitionCN: 以不正确的方式，日常口语中作副词而不加 -ly
senses.example: The spelling went wrong after the first line.
senses.exampleCN: 第一行之后拼写就出错了。
senses.why: English often lets the adjective stand as an adverb, so the crooked thing also describes how the action goes.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让形容词直接充当副词，于是「歪的东西」也用来形容动作的方式。

senses.title: Something done badly
senses.definition: an action that is bad, unfair, or against what is right
senses.definitionCN: 坏的、不公正的或违背正当之事的行为
senses.example: He could not forgive the wrong done to his family.
senses.exampleCN: 他无法原谅家人所受的冤屈。
senses.why: A crooked act is a wrong act, so the adjective hardened into a noun for the deed itself.
senses.whyCN: 歪的行为就是不正当的行为，于是形容词固化成指这种行为本身的名词。

senses.title: To treat unfairly
senses.definition: to treat someone unfairly or treat them as if they had done something bad
senses.definitionCN: 不公正地对待某人，或把坏事归到某人身上
senses.example: She felt wronged by the way the manager spoke to her.
senses.exampleCN: 她觉得经理对她说话的方式冤枉了她。
senses.why: To do a wrong to someone is to make them the victim of the crooked act, so the noun turned into a verb.
senses.whyCN: 对某人做一件错事，就是让他成为歪行的受害者，于是名词又变成动词。

intro.en: Wrong came into English from Old Norse and started with the physical sense of twisted or crooked before it became moral.
intro.cn: wrong 由古诺斯语进入英语，先有「扭的、歪的」这个物理意义，之后才转向道德意义。

items.en: rangr meant twisted, bent out of shape, or contrary.
items.cn: rangr 意为扭的、变形的、反向的。

items.en: Wrong first described crooked things and crooked behaviour in the same breath.
items.cn: wrong 起初同时形容歪的东西与不正的行为。

items.en: The moral sense grew stronger, so wrong came to mean not right in conduct.
items.cn: 道德义逐渐加强，wrong 于是意指行为上不正当。

items.en: The adverb use without -ly settled in everyday speech.
items.cn: 日常口语固定了不加 -ly 的副词用法。

items.en: The verb to wrong, meaning to treat unfairly, comes from the noun.
items.cn: 表示不公正对待的动词 wrong 由名词而来。

note.en: The first group holds the family built on wrong, the second holds words that stand against right or fairness.
note.cn: 第一组收以 wrong 构成的词族，第二组收与「正当、公平」相对的词。

entries.definition: In a mistaken or unfair way.
entries.definitionCN: 错误地；不公正地

entries.definition: Not fair or not legal.
entries.definitionCN: 不当的；非法的

entries.definition: Treated unfairly by someone.
entries.definitionCN: 被冤枉的

entries.definition: Not correct or not true.
entries.definitionCN: 不正确的

entries.definition: Wrong because of a mistake in thinking.
entries.definitionCN: 搞错的；误以为的

entries.definition: Not treating people equally or justly.
entries.definitionCN: 不公平的

normalIntro.en: Wrong keeps the silent w and has no -ly adverb in ordinary speech, which makes it easy to spot in a sentence.
normalIntro.cn: wrong 保留不发音的 w，日常口语里作副词也不加 -ly，因此在句子里很好认。

normal.en: The w is silent, so wrong sounds like rong.
normal.cn: w 不发音，wrong 读起来像 rong。

normal.en: Go wrong means something turns out badly.
normal.cn: go wrong 指事情出了岔子。

normal.en: The wrong number is the phrase you hear on a misdialled phone.
normal.cn: wrong number 是打错电话时听到的那句话。

normal.en: Add -ly for the adverb wrongly, used in careful writing.
normal.cn: 加 -ly 得副词 wrongly，多用于正式文字。

normal.en: The old meaning is twisted, which links wrong to crooked.
normal.cn: 旧义是「扭的」，这把 wrong 与「歪」连在一起。

abstract.en: A sign pointing into a dead end.
abstract.cn: 一块把路指向死胡同的牌子。

abstract.en: A line that will not stay straight no matter how you look at it.
abstract.cn: 无论怎么看都直不起来的一条线。

abstract.en: The moment you realise the key fits the wrong door.
abstract.cn: 你发觉钥匙插错了门的那一刻。

examples.en: I think you gave me the wrong address.
examples.cn: 我想你把地址给我错了。

examples.en: Something went wrong with the engine during the flight.
examples.cn: 飞行途中发动机出了问题。

examples.en: He apologised for wronging her in front of the team.
examples.cn: 他为在团队面前冤枉了她而道歉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「荣昂」——调子唱得荣昂过头，就跑调跑错了。

root: 源自中古英语 wrong，来自古诺斯语 rangr（扭的、歪的、反向的），与 wrangle 有远亲关系；由「歪」引申为「不正确、不正当」。

sensesIntro.en: The crooked line comes first, then the misplaced thing, then the crooked way, then the crooked deed, then the person who suffers it.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是歪的线，再是放错位置的东西，然后是歪的做法，接着是不正当的行为，最后是承受这种行为的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line that bends away from the straight path.
core.cn: 核心意象：偏离直路的一条弯线。

branches.en: The truth branch: a claim that does not match the facts.
branches.cn: 真假分支：与事实不符的说法。

branches.en: The fit branch: a thing in the wrong place or time.
branches.cn: 适配分支：位置或时机不对的事物。

branches.en: The manner branch: the crooked line describes how something is done.
branches.cn: 方式分支：歪线用来形容做事的方式。

branches.en: The deed branch: the crooked act becomes a noun.
branches.cn: 行为分支：歪的行动固化成名词。

branches.en: The justice branch: from the deed to the person forced to bear it.
branches.cn: 公正分支：从行为到被迫承受它的人。

intro.en: Wrong is a single Norse stem that now carries adjective, adverb, noun, and verb uses; suffixes build the rest of its family.
intro.cn: wrong 是单一的诺斯语词干，如今兼作形容词、副词、名词和动词；其余词族靠后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Norse rather than Latin; the entries below are Latin words for crookedness and injustice, not ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 词干来自诺斯语而非拉丁语；下面几条是拉丁语中表示「歪」与「不义」的词，并非祖先。

items.example: The stem serves four parts of speech.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干可作四种词性。

items.example: It appears in wrong, write and wrist.
It forms wrongly, used in formal contexts.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 wrongly，多用于正式场合。

items.example: It forms wrongful, full of injustice.
It forms wrongness, the state of being wrong.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 wrongness，错误的状态。

items.example: Doing names the act, wrong describes it.
items.exampleCN: doing 指明行为，wrong 加以形容。

items.example: It forms wronger, rare but regular.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 wronger，罕见但合乎规则。

items.example: It gives wrongs as a verb form and a noun plural.
items.exampleCN: 它构成动词三单与名词复数。

definition_zh: 克服；战胜；压倒；使受不了
definition_en: to deal successfully with a difficulty, to defeat an opponent, or to make someone helpless with a strong feeling or with fumes and heat
core_image: 一个人顶着风爬到最后一道坡顶，身后是散开的队伍
scene: 山口的雪还没化，队伍里有人喘得说不出话，领队回头指了指前面那道坡。 The team overcame the last steep section just before dark.
sceneCN: 这里 overcame 是「克服」（第 1 个义项：把困难顶过去）；句意为队伍在天黑前越过了最后一段陡坡，画面是山口残雪与喘着气的人。

pos.zh: 克服；战胜；压倒；使受不了

derivatives.zh: 由 overcome 加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「克服者；战胜者」
由 overcome 加 -ing 构成的动名词，义为「克服；战胜的过程」

senses.title: To deal successfully with a difficulty
senses.definition: to succeed in dealing with a problem, obstacle or difficult condition that stands in the way
senses.definitionCN: 成功处理挡在面前的难题、障碍或艰难处境
senses.example: She had to overcome her fear of heights before she could cross the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 她得先克服恐高，才敢走过那座桥。
senses.why: The oldest form of the verb is over plus come, meaning to arrive on top of something; a difficulty is treated as ground a person has to get across, so success is pictured as reaching the other side.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词最早是 over 加 come，意为「来到某物之上」；困难被当成一片必须走过去的土地，所以「克服」在画面上就是走到了对面。

senses.title: To defeat an opponent
senses.definition: to get the better of an enemy or rival in a contest, fight or argument
senses.definitionCN: 在竞赛、打斗或争论中压过对手或敌手
senses.example: He overcame his opponent in three straight sets.
senses.exampleCN: 他连下三盘战胜了对手。
senses.why: If coming over something can mean standing on top of it, the same movement serves for a rival: the winner is the one left standing over the other, and the sporting sense follows.
senses.whyCN: 既然「来到某物之上」可以指站到它上面，同一个动作也能用在对手身上：赢家是最后站着、把对方压在下面的那个人，竞技义就由此而来。

senses.title: To make someone helpless with feeling or fumes
senses.definition: usually in the passive, to affect someone so strongly with emotion, heat or fumes that they lose control of themselves
senses.definitionCN: 常用于被动式，指被情绪、热气或烟味冲击到失去自持
senses.example: She was overcome with relief when the results arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 结果传来时，她松了一口气，几乎站不住。
senses.why: A person who is overcome has been come over by something heavier than a task; the same verb that marks getting on top of a problem marks a feeling getting on top of the person.
senses.whyCN: 被 overcome 的人，是被某种比任务更沉的东西压在上面；同一个动词既表示人爬到问题之上，也表示情绪爬到人之上，被动式于是有了「被压倒」的一面。

senses.title: To come upon suddenly, as in older usage
senses.definition: in older writing, to come upon someone or something suddenly, without the modern idea of winning
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的文字里指突然来到某人或某物身上，不含现代「取胜」的意思
senses.example: A great weariness overcame the travellers at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时，一阵极度的疲惫袭向这些旅人。
senses.why: This is the literal layer that the other senses grew from: over as arrival upon a place, with no struggle yet implied, preserved in a few literary phrases.
senses.whyCN: 这是其余义项生长出来的字面层：over 表示「来到某处之上」，此时还没有争胜的意味，只在少数书面说法里保留下来。

intro.en: Overcome was made inside English from two inherited words, and its history runs from plain arrival to victory and then to being flattened by feeling.
intro.cn: overcome 由两个英语固有词在英语内部合成，词义从「到达」走到「取胜」，再走到「被情绪压垮」。

items.en: Over and come both descend from reconstructed Germanic forms, so the compound belongs to the inherited vocabulary rather than to borrowed Latin.
items.cn: over 与 come 都上溯到重构的日耳曼语形式，所以这个复合词属于固有词汇，不是从拉丁语借来的。

items.en: Old English ofercuman meant to come upon a person or place, and from that contact it also meant to get the better of someone.
items.cn: 古英语 ofercuman 指来到某人或某地之上，又从这种接触引申出压过对方的意思。

items.en: Middle English pushed the verb toward victory in battle and success against an obstacle, while the plain arrival sense faded.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个动词推向战场上的胜利与对障碍的克服，单纯的「到达」义则淡出。

items.en: The passive pattern be overcome with gave the word a new task, describing a person flattened by grief, heat or fumes.
items.cn: 被动结构 be overcome with 给了这个词新任务，用来描述被悲伤、热气或烟味压垮的人。

items.en: Modern English keeps the active sense of mastering a problem and the passive sense of being overwhelmed, plus an archaic use for coming upon.
items.cn: 现代英语保留主动的「解决问题」与被动的「被压倒」，另有一层古旧的「突然降临」用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same verb and other compounds built with over; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of winning and of being overwhelmed.
note.cn: 形近组收同一动词的各种形式，以及用 over 构成的其他复合词；近义组收表示取胜与被压垮的动词。

entries.definition: The past tense of the verb, used for a victory already won.
entries.definitionCN: 这个动词的过去式，用于已经取得的胜利。

entries.definition: The present participle, used for the process still going on.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，用于仍在进行的过程。

entries.definition: To do too much, or to cook something for too long.
entries.definitionCN: 做得过多，或把东西煮得过久。

entries.definition: To put too much weight or too many demands on something.
entries.definitionCN: 给某物加上过重的负担或过多的要求。

entries.definition: To take control of a place or people by force.
entries.definitionCN: 以武力控制某地或某人。

entries.definition: To beat someone in a battle, game or election.
entries.definitionCN: 在战斗、比赛或选举中击败某人。

entries.definition: To deal successfully with a difficulty or obstacle.
entries.definitionCN: 成功处理困难或障碍。

entries.definition: To affect someone so strongly that they cannot think or act.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈影响某人，使其无法思考或行动。

normalIntro.en: The word is over plus come, and its hooks return to that arrival, to the fight, and to the feeling that arrives on top of a person.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 over 加 come，记忆钩子都回到那次「到达」、那场争斗，以及压到人头上的情绪。

normal.en: Over and come are both native Germanic words, so overcome was assembled in English rather than borrowed whole.
normal.cn: over 与 come 都是日耳曼语固有词，所以 overcome 是在英语里拼起来的，不是整体借入的。

normal.en: The oldest sense is arrival, which is why an old sentence can say that weariness overcame someone without any fight.
normal.cn: 最老的一层意思是「到达」，所以旧句里可以说疲惫袭向某人，而不含争斗。

normal.en: Victory is pictured as standing over the other person, and that picture produced the modern sense of defeating.
normal.cn: 胜利被画成站在对方之上，这幅画产出了现代的「击败」义。

normal.en: The passive be overcome with keeps the same downward pressure: the feeling is now the thing on top.
normal.cn: 被动式 be overcome with 保留了同一股向下的压力，只是这回压在上面的是情绪。

normal.en: Overdo and overload share the prefix but not the victory, which shows how far over can stretch.
normal.cn: overdo 与 overload 共用前缀却没有胜负之意，可见 over 能拉得多远。

abstract.en: A climber topping the last ridge with the wind at his back is the word at its plainest.
abstract.cn: 登山者顶着风翻过最后一道山脊，就是这个词最朴素的样子。

abstract.en: A wrestler left standing over his rival turns arrival into victory.
abstract.cn: 摔跤手站在对手之上，把「到达」变成了「取胜」。

abstract.en: A letter read at the door, hand shaking, shows how a feeling can arrive on top of a person.
abstract.cn: 在门口读信、手发抖，说明一种情绪如何压到人身上。

examples.en: She had to overcome her fear of heights before she could cross the bridge.
examples.cn: 她得先克服恐高，才敢走过那座桥。

examples.en: He overcame his opponent in three straight sets.
examples.cn: 他连下三盘战胜了对手。

examples.en: She was overcome with relief when the results arrived.
examples.cn: 结果传来时，她松了一口气，几乎站不住。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧沃康」——欧沃扛着难事往前走，总算跨了过去。

root: overcome 由古英语 ofer（在上、越过）与 cuman（来）合成，原义为「来到……之上」，后引申为「压过、战胜」；两半都是日耳曼语固有词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is arriving on top of something; the senses run from crossing a difficulty, to standing over a rival, to a feeling standing over the person, and back to the old literal arrival.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「来到某物之上」；义项从越过困难，到站到对手之上，到情绪压到人头上，再回到古老的「突然降临」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walker topping the last ridge against the wind, the rest of the group scattered behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人顶着风爬到最后一道山脊，队伍散在他身后。

branches.en: a walker forcing his way up the final slope
branches.cn: 登山者硬撑着爬上最后一段坡

branches.en: a wrestler left standing over his rival
branches.cn: 摔跤手站在对手之上

branches.en: a person reading a letter with a shaking hand
branches.cn: 手抖着读信的人

branches.en: weariness arriving at dusk with no struggle at all
branches.cn: 黄昏时毫无争斗地袭来的疲惫

branches.en: one pressure, once pushed against and once suffered
branches.cn: 同一种压力，一次被顶回去，一次被承受

intro.en: The word joins the Old English prefix for over with the verb to come, then feeds a small family of forms and other over- compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词把古英语中表示「在上」的前缀与动词「来」连在一起，再由它生出几个形式与别的 over 复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is a Germanic compound with no Latin family of its own; Latin super is only a distant relative of the prefix over, not a member of this word's family.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语复合词，本身没有拉丁词族；拉丁语 super 只是前缀 over 的远亲，不算这个词族的成员。

items.meaningCN: 把动词变成名词的词尾
